title: Folarin Balogun’s move to Everton in danger of collapsing due to a failed medical
description: David Moyes is at Hill Dickinson and Goodison Park with the Toffees. Folarin Balogun’s proposed transfer from AS Monaco to Everton is in serious jeopardy of collapsing late on deadline day after the...
fullText:
David Moyes is at Hill Dickinson and Goodison Park with the Toffees. Folarin Balogun's proposed transfer from AS Monaco to Everton is in serious jeopardy of collapsing late on deadline day after the striker failed his medical, according to RMC Sport reporter Fabrice Hawkins.

The two clubs had previously agreed a deal worth €45 million plus €5m in add-ons for the 25-year-old United States international. Personal terms on a four-year contract were also agreed, paving the way for Balogun to make the move to Merseyside. However, complications arose during his medical.

While representatives from AS Monaco and Balogun's camp insist he is fully fit and ready to play, Everton's caution has brought negotiations to a halt. With the transfer window closing soon, the impasse threatens to end what was set to be one of Everton's marquee summer additions.

David Moyes had identified Balogun as a priority to lead the Toffees' attack, especially after Beto's departure to Fiorentina. Missing out on Balogun at this late stage leaves Everton short of striker options.

The ripple effects extend to Monaco, who had planned to reinvest the proceeds from Balogun's sale in late-window targets. The collapse of the €50m deal scuppers their transfer plans. Unless Everton decide to renegotiate or take a calculated risk before the deadline, Balogun is set to remain at Monaco.

Everton were previously linked with a move for Richarlison, but a deal now appears unlikely.

Thierno Barry could now become Everton's undisputed starting striker for 2026/27, giving the Frenchman a major opportunity to prove his worth.

He has already scored four times and recorded an assist in three matches across all competitions this term and will look to add to that tally against Manchester United on Sunday.

title: What awaits USWNT during 2027 Women’s World Cup qualification
description: The USWNT doesn’t need to do much to qualify, but they should not take it for granted.
fullText:
The 2027 Women's World Cup is less than 11 months away as 32 teams will gather in Brazil for the tournament. For the United States women's national team, it's a chance to try and get back to being world champions after their title was snatched in 2023 after holding it for eight years.

Now that the Women's World Cup match schedule has been released, all attention is starting to shift towards qualification. But, what does the USWNT need to do to qualify for the Women's World Cup?

We take a look at the road to the 2027 Women's World Cup and what awaits the USWNT this fall.

The October international window is the final round of friendlies before the qualification tournament. The USWNT, ranked second in the FIFA world rankings, plays a pair of friendlies against Spain, the top ranked team and defending Women's World Cup champions. It's not only a huge pair of matches between the top two ranked teams in the world, but also a barometer test.

Then, the November-December international window is when the 2026 Concacaf W Championship will take place in Texas. The tournament serves as both Women's World Cup qualifying and qualification for the 2028 Olympics. Eight teams (USA, Canada, Mexico, Jamaica, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Haiti, and Panama) will compete in a single elimination tournament over the course of nine days in Mansfield, TX and Houston.

The quarterfinal round is the most important for the USWNT in terms of World Cup qualifying. Should they win their quarterfinal match against El Salvador on Nov. 27, the opening match of the tournament, they will qualify directly for the 2027 Women's World Cup. The four quarterfinal winners earn Concacaf's direct bids to the tournament in Brazil.

Should the unexpected happen and the USWNT loses to El Salvador, they would still have a chance to qualify via a series of playoffs. The four quarterfinal losers will move to the play-in round, as Concacaf has two slots in the FIFA Women's World Cup playoffs in February. To fill those slots, the four quarterfinal losers will play, with the winners moving onto the FIFA playoff. For the USWNT, should they be in the play-in round, they would face the loser of the Jamaica-Costa Rica quarterfinal.

The rest of the 2026 Concacaf W Championship, in addition to crowning the region's champion, will be used for Olympic qualifying. Since the 2028 Olympics will be hosted in Los Angeles, the USWNT has an automatic spot as hosts. The top three teams not named the United States at the Concacaf W Championship will also book their place in the 2028 Olympics.

For the USWNT, winning one match to directly qualify for the Women's World Cup may seem like an easy thing, but the players cannot take it for granted. The team doesn't have to look back that far to see what happens when there's a slip-up in the qualification. In 2010, after losing to Mexico in the semifinals of the Concacaf W Championship, the USWNT needed a FIFA playoff win over Italy to qualify for the 2011 Women's World Cup.

Head coach Emma Hayes wants to leave no doubt and qualify directly this time around so attention can turn towards World Cup preparation. After the October friendlies against Spain are complete, the USWNT will focus on winning the Concacaf W Championship and booking tickets to Brazil in the process.

title: Texas Ex Sebastian Gorzny advances in U.S. Open debut. Here's when he plays Wednesday
description: Former Texas tennis player Sebastian Gorzny made his debut in the 2026 U.S. Open and he advanced to the second round. Here's when you can watch him compete.
fullText:
Former Texas tennis player Sebastian Gorzny made his debut Monday at the U.S. Open and the Longhorn advanced to the second round.

In his first round match against Belgium's Raphael Collignon, Gorzny won 3-6, 6-3, 3-6, 6-3, 7-6. They initially began Sunday but due to weather delay, they finished the four-hour match Monday.

Gorzny graduated from UT in the spring and began playing professional tennis. The Californian is ranked 731st in the world and won two matches in the wild card playoff before getting a main draw in the tournament to start it against 38th-ranked Collingnon.

The 22-year-old won a dramatic fourth set to force a fifth when he won on a double fault after five match points.

Seventh seed Danilil Medvedev is Gorzny's next opponent and they take the court Wednesday.

The unseeded Texas Ex got another hard draw since the Russian is ranked eighth in the world. All matches are available on ESPN+ and a time for the match has not yet been determined.

Born in Irvine, Calif., Gorzny initially committed to play tennis at TCU, ranked the third prospect in the country by tennisrecruiting.net, according to his UT bio. He also participated in the 2022 Wimbledon Junior Doubles Championship.

As a freshman he led the Horned Frogs in dual singles and doubles victories with a record of 17-2 in singles and 18-7 in doubles. As a sophomore he helped TCU secure the 2024 national championship beating Texas, 4-3. He transferred to Texas after the national championship season.

As a junior he went 16-9 in both singles and dual matches and he went 20-6 as a senior. He was named both the 2026 American Collegiate Player Wildcard Playoff singles champion and ITA National Senior Player of the Year.

title: Germany legend Antonio Rüdiger announces international retirement with touching message
description: Real Madrid defender Antonio Rüdiger has announced his retirement from the German national team, 12 years after making his debut, as he looks to open the door to new talent
fullText:
After appearing in three FIFA World Cups and two UEFA European Championships for Germany, legendary defender Antonio Rüdiger has announced his decision to step down from international duty.

The 33-year-old Real Madrid star, who appeared in all four of Germany's World Cup games this summer in North America, where they were knocked out in the Round of 32 by Paraguay on penalties, has been a regular for his country when fit for much of the past 12 years.

But now, with Jürgen Klopp having recently taken over from Julian Nagelsmann as the national team's head coach, it seems Rüdiger believes it's time for him to clear the way for the next wave of talent.

'I was edgy about Welcome to Wrexham, but Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney proved me wrong'

Cristiano Ronaldo's mom misses 'intimate' wedding as marriage certificate details ceremony

"After some time spent reflecting, the moment has come for me to end my career with the national team and clear the way for the young generation," he wrote on social media, via an online translation.

"When I first wore the DFB jersey in 2014, I never could have imagined in my wildest dreams that it would ultimately lead to 86 international matches.

"Even though the big title eluded us at the last tournaments and we had to endure some painful defeats, this time was an incredibly special chapter for me—one that will shape me forever.

"A huge thank you goes to: My teammates: For every shared duel and the camaraderie in the locker room and at the team hotel—and above all, for the friendships that will endure far beyond football.

"The entire coaching and support staff: Thank you for the years of trust and the work behind the scenes. A special thanks goes to Jogi Löw, Hansi Flick, and Julian Nagelsmann, who accompanied and shaped me on my journey with the DFB. But also to my mentor in the youth national teams, Horst Hrubesch.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"And of course, to you fans: Thank you for your support—especially for the unforgettable atmosphere at our home EURO 2024.

"For me, a new chapter now begins, in which I will fully focus on my club. Thank you for the shared journey. Your Toni."

Rüdiger retires having scored three goals and provided five assists during his tenure with the national team, with whom he won the Confederations Cup in 2017 and reached the EURO 2024 quarter-finals.

He can now focus solely on his club career with Madrid, which he has called home since leaving Chelsea after five seasons back in 2022. A two-time Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup, and Copa del Rey champion - amongst numerous other accolades with both the Blues and Los Blancos - Rüdiger was an unused substitute for Madrid's first two La Liga games this season, but played the full 90 in their recent 4-0 win against Málaga CF.

Led once more by José Mourinho, who returned to the Spanish capital this summer for what is his second stint in charge of Madrid, his side has won all three of their league games to date, leaving them second in the standings behind reigning champions Barcelona on goal difference. Next up is a trip to seventh-placed Real Betis on Friday.

title: Breakaway Holiday Classic will feature five high school games, three state finalists
description: The high school basketball Breakaway Holiday Classic will be five-game event at Noblesville's Riverview Health Arena
fullText:
The second annual Breakaway Holiday Classic presented by Citizens State Bank will feature five high school basketball games, including three state finalists from last season.

The event will be played at Riverview Health Arena on Jan. 2. Tickets will go on sale Sept. 23. Here is a look at the matchups:

Sheridan is coming off a 19-5 season and will return all-state senior Trey Page, who averaged 19.3 points per game last season and shot 39% from the 3-point line. Seniors Desh Donathan and John Crowder also return. Sheridan is a Class 2A program. Liberty Christian went 19-8 last season, falling in a 2-point game in the semistate to eventual Class 1A state champion Barr-Reeve. The Lions should again be one of the top teams in 1A with Kendrick Martin (17.8 ppg, 4.5 rebounds) and others returning.

Both teams played in the state finals last season. Barr-Reeve went 28-1 and won the Class 1A state title, while Westview came up just short against Parke Heritage in the 2A game, falling 57-56. Barr-Reeve returns all five starters from last year's team, including senior Kierson Lengacher (14.0 ppg) and juniors Jaylon Graber (10.8 ppg, 4.0 rebounds) and Braxton Neidigh (9.9 ppg). Westview brings back senior standout Austin Schlabach (19.5 ppg, 5.7 assists), a Huntington commit.

"We are excited for our matchup against a historic program like Barr-Reeve. It should be a great battle between two really good programs," Westview coach Chandler Prible said.

Lawrence North is coming off four consecutive seasons of at least 18 wins. This team will be a little on the young side with juniors Chandon Gilbert (10.2 ppg) and Davis Baker (6.0 ppg, 40.4% 3-pointers) the top returning scorers. Talked freshman Levin Robinson will also be a key player for Lawrence North. Fort Wayne Snider will return four starters from a 20-8 squad, including Trell Hogue (11.5 ppg), Ketron Paschall (8.8 ppg, 6.5 rebounds) and Chance DeRossett (8.3 ppg, 3.4 rebounds).

"We are so excited to be able to play a great opponent in a professional arena. These are the type of games that help prepare a team for the tournament and we are excited to test ourselves with a high-level opponent," Snider coach Joshua Riikonen said.

Guerin is coming off a 21-6 season and returns four starters for a squad that should be among the best in Class 3A. Jake Grissom (20.5 ppg, 4.5 rebounds), a Junior All-Star last season, will lead the Golden Eagles, along with seniors Carter Murans (12.4 ppg, 4.6 rebounds) and Hayden Rogers (8.1 ppg, 7.0 assists). New Albany, a 23-6 regional champion last season, will bring back four starters and nine players with experience, including junior standout Noah Washington (18.2 ppg), senior Reece McKee (15.3 ppg) and sophomore Karson Stoudemire (17.0 ppg). The Bulldogs were one step away from the state finals last season, falling to eventual state champion Mt. Vernon in the semistate championship.

"We are excited to be included in an event that features some of the best teams in Indiana and thankful for the opportunity to play in one of the premier venues in Hamilton County," Guerin coach Sam Gardner said. "We have great respect for Coach Jones and a New Albany team that will be a 4A title contender this year."

The nightcap will feature two top 4A programs. Crown Point is coming off a trip to the 4A state finals last season and will bring back one of the top juniors in the state in 6-5 guard M.J. Wilson. The Bulldogs were 25-2 last season. Hamilton Southeastern is coming off a 15-10 season last year and brings back junior Varschon Clark (13.3 ppg, 4.6 rebounds) and sophomore K.J. Buckley (3.3 ppg), among others.

"Crown Point is thrilled and honored to be playing in the 2027 Breakaway Holiday Classic. The opportunity to play a great program like Hamilton Southeastern in a venue like Riverview Health Arena are just the type of opportunities we seek out for our players," said Crown Point coach Clint Swan. "It promises to be a great day of basketball and a memorable experience for all."

title: Former Cowboys QB Tony Romo pleads no contest to OWI, addresses alcohol struggles
description: Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo pleaded no contest to OWI following his July arrest in Milwaukee and addressed his struggles with alcohol.
fullText:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo pleaded no contest Tuesday to operating while intoxicated in connection with his July arrest in Milwaukee, according to WISN 12.

Romo, 46, will have his driver's license revoked for six months and must pay a $784 fine. He also must complete an alcohol assessment program and install an ignition interlock device on any vehicle he owns.

Milwaukee County sheriff's deputies arrested Romo, a Wisconsin native, on July 23 after a traffic stop.

According to a search warrant obtained by WISN 12, a deputy reported smelling a "strong odor of an alcoholic beverage" on Romo's breath. Body-camera footage showed Romo telling the deputy he had not consumed any alcohol.

ALSO READ: Dear Dallas Cowboys, please make the Super Bowl again before I die

Citations obtained by WISN 12 state that deputies found an open bottle of an alcoholic beverage on the passenger side of Romo's vehicle. Court records also show he was cited for refusing an intoxication test and first-offense operating while intoxicated.

In Wisconsin, a first-offense OWI is generally treated as a civil traffic violation rather than a criminal offense.

Romo addressed the case in an Instagram statement Tuesday, saying he took responsibility for his actions.

"This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWI in Wisconsin," Romo said. "I own this completely."

Romo said multiple back surgeries following his NFL career left him with persistent pain and led to a dependence on pain medication. His efforts to stop using the medication eventually contributed to an over-reliance on alcohol, he said, while emphasizing that it did not excuse his actions.

Romo is currently on leave from CBS Sports, where he is part of the network's lead NFL broadcast team. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that former Wisconsin Badgers and NFL star J.J. Watt will fill in during Romo's absence.

Romo spent his entire 14-year NFL career with the Cowboys, earning four Pro Bowl selections before retiring after the 2016 season and joining CBS.

There's more to San Antonio with the Express-News.

title: Tom Brady's sports memorabilia store to open in downtown Indianapolis
description: CardVault by Tom Brady will open at a central downtown corner this fall, bringing the former quarterback's brand to Indiana.
fullText:
Tom Brady will be setting up shop in Indianapolis. No, not on the football team.

CardVault by Tom Brady, a sports and trading cards, collectibles and memorabilia shop co-founded by the former Patriots quarterback, will open at 2 W. Washington St. in downtown Indianapolis later this year, said Nick Wright, who leases retail spaces on the building's ground floor.

The company signed a 10-year lease in the building known as the H.P. Wasson & Company Building.

CardVault leadership wants to open the Indianapolis store as soon as possible, Wright said. The initial plans called for opening by the first Colts home game, slated for Sunday, Sept. 13, but that's not likely to happen.

Wright deferred IndyStar to CardVault for more specific information on the grand opening, which Wright said Brady will likely attend. IndyStar's attempts to contact CardVault before publication were unsuccessful.

CardVault was established during the pandemic in 2020. Since then, the brand has become one of the fastest growing collectibles retail stores in the country, opening in "major cities near iconic venues," according to CardVault's website.

Currently, CardVault operates 17 brick-and-mortar stores alongside a handful of vending machine operations in Los Angeles, Boston and Minneapolis, where it sells sports memorabilia and trading cards brands, such as Pokémon. Inside, collectors can also submit items for grading.

CardVault's rise builds on a booming, multi-billion-dollar collectibles industry that has brought increased attention to the hobby of sports and trading cards. The industry is projected to be worth nearly $7 billion by 2035.

The store's spot in Indianapolis taps into the dedicated sports community, the annual presence of Gen Con at the convention center and regional sports shows, like the National Sports Collectors Convention held in Chicago earlier this summer.

Across the country, CardVault has been experimenting with setting up shop in downtown areas.

"It'll be a great place for people to get together and trade," Wright said of the Indianapolis store. "I'm really, really looking forward to seeing collectors, sports fans, visitors come together in this space. It's good for downtown and the growing collectibles industry."

The storefront on the northwest corner of the Meridian and Washington streets intersection has not been available for nearly two decades, Wright said. T-Mobile moved out of the space earlier this month. When the company moved out, Wright wanted to veer away from the typical coffee shop or restaurant space, aiming to bring an "experiential" store to the high-trafficked and visible corner.

Wright described CardVault as a win-win for downtown retail and the collectibles industry in Indianapolis.

"It says a lot about Indianapolis," Wright said.

title: LA Rams’ 8.5-Sack Starter’s Role in Jeopardy After Aaron Donald Comeback
description: The Los Angeles Rams aquired one of the most accomplished defensive players in NFL history when Aaron Donald ended his retirement.But the reunion could come with a tradeoff for a young linemen who helped replace him.Braden Fiske, a 2024 second-round pick who burst onto the scene with a team-high 8.5 sacks as a rookie, now […] The post LA Rams’ 8.5-Sack Starter’s Role in Jeopardy After Aaron Donald Comeback appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams aquired one of the most accomplished defensive players in NFL history when Aaron Donald ended his retirement.

But the reunion could come with a tradeoff for a young linemen who helped replace him.

Braden Fiske, a 2024 second-round pick who burst onto the scene with a team-high 8.5 sacks as a rookie, now faces a potentially smaller role in a deeper Rams front.

Sports Illustrated's Blaine Grisak identified Fiske as one of three "losers" from the Rams' initial 53-man roster, pointing directly to Donald's return as the development that could alter Fiske's standing in the defensive-line rotation.

The concern centers less on Fiske's place on the roster and more on how many opportunities remain available after Los Angeles dropped a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year into an already full-capacity group.

Grisak wrote that Fiske "hasn't flashed this summer" and has "taken a step back since his rookie season." He added that a reduced role could ultimately help Fiske while simultaneously limiting his overall roof.

There's statistical context behind that assessment.

Fiske recorded 44 tackles, 8.5 sacks and two forced fumbles across 17 games as a rookie, starting eight. His sack total led the Rams during the 2024 regular season and established him as one of the team's most promising young pass rushers.

His conventional production dipped in Year 2.

Fiske started 16 of 17 games in 2025 but finished with 30 tackles and three sacks. He also went without a forced fumble after producing two during his rookie campaign.

The sack decline didn't erase his effectiveness as a pass rusher. Pro Football Focus credited Fiske with 42 pressures on 365 pass-rush snaps last season, which ranked 16th among interior defenders. He added eight quarterback hits and 31 hurries.

That profile could make Fiske particularly convenient in a rotation assembled to keep Donald fresh.

Donald returned at 35 after spending two seasons away from football. The Rams began ramping him up in practice after his Aug. 30 return, while Donald said he still believes he can play at a high level.

Even a managed workload for Donald creates a numbers crunch inside.

Los Angeles enters 2026 with more defensive-line firepower than it had when Donald retired following the 2023 season.

Fiske has compiled 11.5 sacks and 93 pressures through his first 34 regular-season games, per his official Rams biography. Rather than asking him to handle the workload that came with 16 starts last season, the Rams can pick their spots and deploy him as part of a deeper rotation.

That may prove valuable after Fiske's sophomore sack total fell by more than half.

Donald returns with 111 career sacks, 176 tackles for loss and 790 pressures, according to the Rams' official team website.

Even if Los Angeles manages his snaps, his presence figures to command considerable attention from opposing offensive lines and generate more favorable matchups elsewhere, so Fiske could become one of the primary beneficiaries.

Grisak acknowledged that possibility despite placing Fiske on the losing side of the roster fallout, suggesting a smaller role alongside Donald could help the third-year defender.

For a player who produced 8.5 sacks when he carried a lighter starting burden as a rookie, fewer snaps don't necessarily mean less impact. Nonetheless, the challenge will be making those opportunities count.

Donald's comeback may lower Fiske's projected workload. But the 26-year-old may edge toward rediscovering the disruptive form that made his rookie season stand out.

title: Cowboys want Joe Milton back on the practice squad
description: In a bit of a surprise move, the Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton on Monday.
fullText:
In a bit of a surprise move, the Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton on Monday. They hope to sign him back to the practice squad.

Dallas named Sam Howell the backup to Dak Prescott and left Milton temporarily out of work after the Cowboys claimed running back Emari Demercado and needed a roster spot.

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer and executive vice president Stephen Jones both said Tuesday that they want Milton back on the practice squad as the team's third quarterback. Milton's departure would necessitate signing a different third quarterback.

The Cowboys are waiting to see if Milton clears waivers.

"Joe obviously played really good in the preseason games," Jones said on All DLLS Cowboys. "We really liked his performance. Sam did as well. But at the end of the day, when you took the full body of work in training camp, the practices against other teams, the coaches thought — albeit really close — Sam was the best choice for the team to go with as two now. We'd love to have Joe back. A lot of teams in this league figure out ways to carry three and four [quarterbacks]. We've got a lot of stress on our roster with this new defense and things that we're doing that we can carry two [quarterbacks]. We're in talks with Joe. We'll see if he gets claimed. If he doesn't, we'd love to have Joe back as our three and on the practice squad."

In three preseason games, Milton completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He added 12 carries for 14 yards and a rushing touchdown.

The Cowboys traded a fifth-round pick to New England for Milton in the 2025 offseason, and he served as Prescott's backup last season.

title: Mike Norvell updates status of FSU's injured DBs, WRs
description: Mike Norvell provided an update on Jordan Crutchfield, Chuck Kennon, Devin Carter, and Tae'Shaun Gelsey ahead of FSU's game vs. SMU.
fullText:
While all of FSU's starters played in the season-opening win over the New Mexico State Aggies, several depth pieces were limited or unavailable for the Seminoles.

True freshman defensive back Jordan Crutchfield was praised by FSU's coaching staff during fall camp, and he made his debut in the 34-17 win. However, he was limited to just six snaps before leaving with an injury. Head coach Mike Norvell confirmed FSU is monitoring his status ahead of their Week 1 game against the No. 19 SMU Mustangs.

"Jordan came out at this time we're continuing to monitor and evaluate what that's going to look like forthis week, but you're very hopeful and kind of see where that plays out as the week progresses," Norvell said.

He also addressed the status of true freshman cornerback Chuck Kennon, who was FSU's highest-rated signee in the 2026 recruiting class but did not dress for the game.

"We'll see where Chuck is. He was out in the last game. He's dealing with nothing major, but he's working through a slight injury. We'll continue to see how he progresses with that."

The Seminoles were also down two wideouts in sophomore Tae'Shaun Gelsey and true freshman Devin Carter. Norvell is expecting to get Gelsey "back this week," while they are seeing "where things go" with Carter.

The game between FSU and SMU is set to kick off Monday at 7:30 p.m. ET at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Florida. It is the first time that the two programs have ever played in Tallahassee.

title: Boxing stock watch: August's biggest winners and losers after Moses Itauma's disaster, Teofimo Lopez's revival
description: A new heavyweight champion, a three-division king and a pair of costly setbacks headlined a wild month in the sweet science.
fullText:
Green Day's Billie Joe Armstrong famously told us to wake up when September starts, right?

OK, maybe it's when it ends, but if you think I'll remember to use that opener in a month's time then you are seriously overestimating my memory.

So here we are. The nights are drawing in, summer feels like a long-lost relative and we have winners and losers to dish out from a fairly busy August, a month usually pencilled in for summer holidays and bare boxing cupboards.

Who won and lost the month of August 2026? Keep scrolling to find out.

"Coming to London against all odds, 34 years, and making this. It's incredible."

These were the words of the newly crowned IBF heavyweight world champion, Filip Hrgovic, moments after upsetting Moses Itauma inside London's O2 Arena. And he's not wrong: it was incredible.

The Croatian was outboxed from the first round until an unforgettable ninth, where his Olympics-schooled nous and championship fighting experience paid dividends, capitalizing on an exhausted Itauma to leave the referee no choice but to stop the contest.

Hrgovic is the toast of Croatia and another new champion in a heavyweight division that is changing its guard. It's the division that just keeps on giving, and with four different beltholders and a slew of contenders knocking at the door, we are in for a fun few years.

Speaking of heavyweight, the division is due a new boogeyman.

Teremoana has been given the big push from Matchroom Boxing and Eddie Hearn over the past 18 months, half out of genuine expectation of his high-talent ceiling, and half out of necessity seeing as Frank Warren appears to have every other heavyweight on the planet.

He extended his winning run in August to 12-0 (12 KOs), pulverizing American DeAndre Savage inside two uncompetitive rounds, and sticking his flag in the division as a player in the next generation of heavyweight stars.

Time will tell. History tells us that if you're big and you can punch, then you have a very good chance of succeeding in this volatile division.

Forget boogeyman. Teremoana is looking to be the man.

"I need to tell you guys, if you lose and you come back, then you never lost because you're a winner," Teofimo Lopez said after toppling Rolly Romero to become a three-division world champion.

"I'm a winner. I'm a true example of what winning is, and it ain't about losing. It's about never giving up."

Well, that's all very well and good, Teo, but just tell that to the January version of this column where you were very much listed as a loser following a one-sided loss to Shakur Stevenson.

But give credit where credit is due. Lopez bounced back well in Las Vegas, holding up well in his welterweight debut and edging out the former champion Romero — 116-112, 115-113 and 114-114 — on the scorecards.

Lopez's success came due to a clever jab and good in-ring movement against a bigger guy and puncher in Romero, and this will surely give him confidence that he can be a big face in the star-studded land of 147-pounders.

Just don't mention Jack Catterall.

Not only did Dina Thorslund return to the sport as a winner in August, the Danish two-weight world champion was punch perfect in her undisputed bantamweight title win over Cherneka Johnson.

It'd been just over a year after vacating her WBC and WBO bantamweight titles following the announcement of her pregnancy, but the 32-year-old fought in the MVPW-05 main event in Orlando like she'd never been away.

This win has propelled the 118-pounder to the top of the division and into a No. 6 spot in Uncrowned's latest women's boxing pound-for-pound rankings.

Zuffa Boxing 10 landed on Irish shores in August, as Dublin's 3Arena hosted big wins for the pair of middleweights Aaron McKenna and Callum Walsh.

McKenna was crowned the IBF champion at 160 pounds after a unanimous decision win over Etinosa Oliha, while Walsh continued his push in the division, beating Tyler Denny over 10 rounds.

Ireland has been calling out for a bonafide superstar to carry the men's side of the sport, and thoughts could possibly be turning to a future clash between the Monaghan and Cork fighters. With Stephen McKenna — Aaron's younger brother — also in the mix at middleweight, future options are plentiful.

"It's a big time for Irish boxing," Walsh explained. "As an Irish fighter from such a small place, there are three of us now in Zuffa Boxing."

We don't like sulkers over here at Uncrowned.

After losing his WBA welterweight strap to Teofimo Lopez in a tight majority decision, Rolly Romero gave us an early exit, leaving the ring on his own with a face like thunder.

Whether fighters should have a camera and microphone shoved in their face after 36 minutes of energy-zapping, head-pummeling action is an entirely separate conversation, but nevertheless, the optics inside the T-Mobile Arena weren't great for the fallen champion.

"I got hit with two punches the whole fight that barely grazed me," said Romero, despite CompuBox recording 124 punches to Romero's 73. "I was never in any trouble. When I heard 114-114, I knew it was a robbery."

When The Specials released the song "Too Much Too Young" in January 1980, it's unlikely they were predicting the future of the heavyweight boxing landscape, and the UK's next big heavyweight hope Moses Itauma falling short at his first world title attempt.

But that's what happened to the 21-year-old in August, as he failed to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion in history after Filip Hrgovic wore him down in the ninth round of their London blockbuster.

Boxing teaches the toughest lessons. Itauma will, of course, come again, but it's a stark reminder that the sport isn't fought with records nor on paper.

Itauma was a huge betting favorite coming into this one, but the occasion — as well as a tough hard-hitting Croatian — got the better of him, as he visibly struggled to breathe enough of the hot air from inside the O2 Arena into his lungs.

He's a loser this month, but one suspects that he'll be a big winner multiple times across the rest of his career.

Mikaela Mayer failed to get the rub of the green again on British shores at the end of August, dropping the third loss of his career — all in the UK — to Chantelle Cameron for the WBA and WBC super welterweight titles.

Cameron was impressive in her aggression against Mayer, with unrelenting pressure nullifying Mayer's in-ring smarts, eventually winning the argument 97-93 on two scorecards and 96-94 on the other.

In the ring afterward, Mayer was adamant she had done enough to win, suggesting Cameron was "lucky" the fight had taken place in the UK as the pair exchanged tense words. The American later reflected on the moment, taking to social media to apologize for what she described as "poor sportsmanship."

I want to apologize for my poor sportsmanship last night. My emotions got the best of me. I have not re watched the fight yet but when I do I will make an honest assessment and be sure to fix my mistakes in this next camp.

Congratulations to @chantellecam on the win. It was an…

OK, it's probably time that we draw a line under this one. If Fury vs. Joshua isn't announced in September, then let's just call it a day, lads.

August saw little progression in an agreement to get this "Battle of Britain" over the line, with location and reported unpaid bills from the Saudis to Matchroom and Joshua being the two biggest sticking points.

Either way, it's an awful look for two British heavyweights that are dangerously close to being remembered for a fight that didn't happen, rather than two glittering careers.

title: Midfielder Lee leaves Wrexham by mutual consent
description: Midfielder Elliot Lee, a three-time promotion winner with Wrexham, leaves the Championship club by mutual consent.
fullText:
Wrexham have terminated the contract of midfielder Elliot Lee by mutual consent.

The 31-year-old joined the Red Dragons from Luton Town in the summer of 2022 and played a starring role in the club's rapid rise up the football pyramid.

Lee recently entered the final year of his deal with Wrexham and departs the Racecourse Ground having scored 41 goals and featured 152 times across all competitions for the north Wales side.

Manager Phil Parkinson said: "I'd like to thank Elliot for what he has done for this football club.

"He has been a great player for us here at Wrexham and has made a significant contribution to the club's rise through the divisions.

"He is at the stage now where he is eager to go and play and get some minutes, and whoever gets him will get a player who still has a lot to offer."

Wrexham seal signing of Sheffield United's O'Hare

Sheff Utd stance 'natural' in Wrexham's O'Hare bid

Lee featured prominently as Wrexham gained three successive promotions from the National League to the Championship.

He was named in the 2022-23 National League team of the year as Wrexham clinched the fifth-tier title with a record 111 points.

The midfielder was listed in the League Two team of the season and the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) team of the year in the following campaign as Wrexham sealed automatic promotion into League One.

The West Ham United academy product's influence waned following Wrexham's promotion into the Championship last year.

Lee's three appearances for the club last season all came in the EFL Cup, and he went on to join Doncaster Rovers on loan where he featured 18 times in League One.

The Durham-born player has not featured in any of Wrexham's four matchday squads across all competitions so far this season and is now a free agent.

He has reportedly attracted interest from League One side Sheffield Wednesday.

title: Jaguars 2026 practice squad tracker: Did J’Mari Taylor make the B team?
description: Practice squad invites are about to go out!
fullText:
With roster cuts beginning for the Jacksonville Jaguars and every other NFL team, practice squad invitations will be sent out shortly. Here's a brief primer from our friends at Field Gulls. Keep track of who the Jags add to their practice squad below!

Teams can begin forming their practice squads after the waiver period expires at 1 p.m. ET on Monday, August 31. The NFL will send a subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, and teams can begin signing practice squad players after receiving that notice.

A player claimed off waivers cannot go directly to a practice squad. A successful waiver claim means that player goes onto the claiming team's 53-man roster. The player must first clear waivers before becoming eligible to sign with a practice squad.

A standard practice squad consists of 16 players. Teams can have a 17th player if that player qualifies for and is designated under the NFL's International Player Pathway Program (Jacksonville may keep OL Kilian Zierer in this spot).

Players who are not subject to waivers can immediately sign with another team or join a practice squad. Players with four or more accrued seasons are unrestricted free agents when released and are not subject to waivers. Players with three or fewer accrued seasons are subject to the waiver process.

OL Kilian Zierer (International Pathway Program)

According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Jaguars have +3000 odds to win Super Bowl LXI.

title: ‘Should Never Play for Team US Again’ – WNBA World Reacts As USA Head Coach Shrugs Off A’ja Wilson Absence Question
description: Team USA released its roster and schedule for the 2026 FIBA Women’s World Cup on Tuesday, and although most of the women were expected to be on the roster, there were a few moves (or non-moves) that drew questions. Although the likes of Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, and Angel Reese will be playing for Team USA, it came as a surprise to many that Team USA will be without Las Vegas Aces’ star A’Ja Wilson.
fullText:
Team USA released its roster and schedule for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup on Tuesday, and although most of the women were expected to be on the roster, there were a few moves (or non-moves) that drew questions.
Although the likes of Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, and Angel Reese will be playing for Team USA, it came as a surprise to many that Team USA will be without Las Vegas Aces' star A'Ja Wilson.

Wilson, the number one overall pick of the 2018 draft, is having another outstanding season, averaging 26.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.0 blocks, and 1.4 steals in 32.0 minutes per game.

Wilson is shooting 52.3% from the field and 39.8% from three. Wilson is a three-time WNBA champion, two-time Finals MVP, eight-time All-Star, three-time Defensive Player of the Year, and four-time MVP.

Simply put, she is one of, if not the, best player in the WNBA right now, so it's clear why her absence has drawn so many questions.

Another mainstay, Kelsey Plum of the Phoenix Mercury, also won't be playing due to injury. Team USA head coach Kara Lawson gave her reaction to the news.

"Both of them [Kelsey Plum included] obviously have been great players for us, and I'll miss being around them, but ultimately, we've kind of moved on…" Lawson said. "We don't have time to be worried about who's not here. We've got to really focus on ourselves."

That's the only kind of mindset that Lawson can have at this time. Of course, with an incredible roster still miles more talented and deeper than any other country, it's probably easy to get over a couple of key players missing the tournament.

Lawson addressed several issues but said she had not spoken with A'ja Wilson about her decision not to play in the World Cup. Sue Bird apparently handled that.

"I didn't have any conversation with A'ja (Wilson)," Lawson said.

Wilson certainly isn't required to play in the tournament, but not having a conversation with Lawson prior to the decision becoming public is definitely going to strike some the wrong way. The CDS Sports Podcast weighed in and had nothing kind to say about Wilson's decision.

"Like I said, A'ja Wilson is garbage," they wrote on X. "Not even having a conversation with the coach is trash behavior. What a scumbag. She should never play for Team US again. She's a dinosaur & fake 'star' anyway. She's Angel Reese with a better whistle."

Obviously, they may have gone a little far, but you can see the anger is there. Coach Anderson thinks Lawson is upset with Wilson's choice.

They wrote: "Damn! Kara Lawson seems upset about A'ja Wilson quitting on her team so late!"

Whether it's quitting on the team is debatable, but you can see why Lawson may be upset. Leena points out that no one really knows why Wilson isn't playing.

"So is Aja sick or injured? I'm so confused on how nobody from Team USA knows what's going on with her?"they asked. It's an interesting question, and the uncertainty will only lead to more questions and speculation.

Shraddha thinks Wilson should have been more 'professional.' "That sounds bad," they said. "A'ja was not professional about it at all."

All in all, this does not seem like it was handled well on Wilson's part, and that's only going to add fuel to the fan's fire.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Deadline day: Man City agree joint British record Enzo Fernandez move
description: Chelsea have agreed to sell midfielder Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125 million ($169 million) as Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo prepare to make deadline-day moves to rivals Tottenham Hotspur. With the 11pm (2200 GMT) deadline fast approaching, the Press Association understands a British record-equalling deal has been struck to take the Argentina international to the Etihad Stadium.
fullText:
Chelsea have agreed to sell midfielder Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125 million ($169 million) as Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo prepare to make deadline-day moves to rivals Tottenham Hotspur.

With the 11pm (2200 GMT) deadline fast approaching, the Press Association understands a British record-equalling deal has been struck to take the Argentina international to the Etihad Stadium.

The size of the fee for Fernandez matches that paid by Liverpool to Newcastle for Alexander Isak a year ago and sees Fernandez join his former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca at City.

Chelsea's eye-catching transfer business continues elsewhere, with defender Adarabioyo set to leave Stamford Bridge for Spurs along with Mudryk as he reunites with his former Shakhtar Donetsk coach Roberto De Zerbi.

Mudryk joined Chelsea in an £89 million deal in 2023 and in July came back from a 20-month suspension after returning an adverse finding for the banned substance meldonium in 2024.

The loan deal is understood to include the option to make the move permanent for £75 million, while Adarabioyo is set to switch for £7 million - a deal that has seen Kevin Danso join Sunderland.

The Austria international moves to the Stadium of Light on loan with an obligation for the deal to become permanent if certain performance related conditions are met.

Marc Guiu has already completed his Chelsea exit, joining RB Leipzig for £14.5 million, while Dario Essugo and and Deivid Washington have joined sister club Strasbourg on loan and permanent deals respectively.

The Blues have also agreed a deal to sign 18-year-old defender Honest Ahanor from Atalanta next summer, but the defender will spend this season in the Premier League on loan at Crystal Palace.

Works continues at rebuilding Aston Villa, with winger Ibrahim Mbaye joining from Paris Saint-Germain in a reported club-record £47 million deal on deadline day.

Unai Emery's men have also acquired England defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Championship promotion hopefuls Southampton in a move rising to £30 million.

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott, who endured a nightmare loan spell at Villa Park last term, has joined LaLiga outfit Valencia for the season.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo has arrived at Newcastle from Lille for £51 million, while Nick Woltemade has joined Juventus on a season-long loan. Tottenham's Pape Matar Sarr also moved to the Turin club on deadline day on an initial loan.

Everton have agreed a deal to take Jack Grealish on another season-long loan from Manchester City, PA understands, having impressed there last term before suffering a season-ending foot injury in January.

The deal for Grealish to return to Everton comes at the same time as City have agreed a fee worth up to £65 million for Toffees winger Iliman Ndiaye. Everton have sold striker Beto to Serie A side Fiorentina for an undisclosed fee.

Arsenal have sold Brazil striker Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona, where he has penned a three-year deal.

Fabio Vieira has joined Hamburg on a permanent deal after spending last season there and Ethan Nwaneri has joined Borussia Dortmund on loan.

United are in discussions to sign Leicester teenager Louis Page, PA understands, while Sunderland and Crystal Palace are vying for the signature of Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

Premier League surprise package Hull look set for a busy evening, having already signed striker Ilyas Ansah from Bundesliga side Union Berlin for an undisclosed fee.

Work is afoot to bring in other players and others could be shifted out, including Saturday's matchwinner Liam Millar.

title: Saints sign former Browns, Tennessee Vols WR to practice squad
description: The New Orleans Saints are up to seven WR between their practice squad and 53-man roster after signing former Browns third-round pick Cedric Tillman.
fullText:
This could be interesting. The New Orleans Saints are up to seven wide receivers between their practice squad and 53-man roster after signing former Cleveland Browns third-round pick Cedric Tillman. And we're still waiting to find out of Kevin Austin Jr. cleared waivers and will be returning to the practice squad, too. But what's Tillman's story?

Tillman, 26, played college football at Tennessee (arriving in 2018, one year after Alvin Kamara turned pro) and was prolific in Josh Heupel's wide-open passing attack. He broke out in 2021 with 64 catches for 1,081 yards and a dozen touchdowns before taking as step back in 2022 while dealing with an ankle injury. The Saints passed on him to pick running back Kendre Miller at No. 71 overall in the 2023 draft, but he went off the board to Cleveland just a few slots later at No. 74.

Injuries and inconsistent play have been a problem for Tillman in the NFL. He's been limited to 38 of 51 possible games since the Browns drafted him, and while his raw numbers look promising (71 receptions for 833 yards and five touchdowns), he has yet to post a 100-yard game in the NFL. In per-game averages, he's put up 1.9 receptions per game and 21.9 yards per game. Some of that can be attributed to the Browns' terrible quarterback situation. But not all of it.

Maybe a change of scenery is just what he needs. But for now, Tillman is one of three wideouts on the practice squad, along with Trey Palmer (returning from last year's team) and Jalen Moreno-Cropper. Between Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele, Bryce Lance and Barion Brown standing on top of the depth chart, it's going to be tough for any of them to see meaningful reps in Week 1.

title: Former Heisman winner could see his son playing for Marcus Freeman

fullText:
Over the last few recruiting cycles, Notre Dame has become a place that attracts former NFL and college players son's, both legacy's and non.

Larry Fitzgerald, an NFL Hall of Famer, who went to Pittsburgh has his son enrolled, as do multiple former Irish players like the Flanigan family. There could be another football legacy to play in South Bend, and one that might be like the Fitzgerald's as former Heisman Trophy winner Mark Ingram is a big fan of Notre Dame.

Ingram won the Heisman Trophy in 2009 with Alabama, went on the be a first-round NFL draft selection and played in the NFL for twelve years before retiring following the 2022 season. It is still a few more years until Ingraham's son is ready to be recruited, and if Freeman is still in South Bend, there's a good chance that he ends up playing for Notre Dame.

Alabama Hesiman, Mark Ingram² says he knows where legacies go to play football and makes his case for his son going to Notre Dame.

title: Real Madrid star announces international retirement
description: A leading member of the defensive ranks at La Liga heavyweights Real Madrid has on Tuesday called time on his playing career at international level. The Blancos star in question? Antonio Rüdiger.Stop...
fullText:
A leading member of the defensive ranks at La Liga heavyweights Real Madrid has on Tuesday called time on his playing career at international level. The Blancos star in question? Antonio Rüdiger.

Stopper Rüdiger for his part featured prominently this summer, as the German national team made the trip to North America for the 2026 World Cup. All told, the former Chelsea man played his part in all four of his nation's fixtures.

After another difficult campaign for Die Mannschaft, culminating in a Round-of-32 exit at the hands of Paraguay, however, Rüdiger has made the call to bring down the curtain on his career with Germany.

As per a lengthy statement across the official social media platforms of the 33-year-old on Tuesday:

'After some time spent reflecting, the moment has come for me to end my career with the national team and clear the way for the young generation. When I first wore the DFB jersey in 2014, I never could have imagined in my wildest dreams that it would ultimately lead to 86 international matches. Even though the big title eluded us at the last tournaments and we had to endure some painful defeats, this time was an incredibly special chapter for me—one that will shape me forever.

A huge thank you goes to: My teammates: For every shared duel and the camaraderie in the locker room and at the team hotel—and above all, for the friendships that will endure far beyond football. The entire coaching and support staff: Thank you for the years of trust and the work behind the scenes. A special thanks goes to Jogi Löw, Hansi Flick, and Julian Nagelsmann, who accompanied and shaped me on my journey with the DFB. But also to my mentor in the youth national teams, Horst Hrubesch. And of course, to you fans: Thank you for your support—especially for the unforgettable atmosphere at our home EURO 2024.

For me, a new chapter now begins, in which I will fully focus on my club. Thank you for the shared journey.

Rüdiger closes out his international career with an impressive 86 caps, with a FIFA Confederations Cup, won back in 2017, to show for his efforts.

title: Five surprises from Vanderbilt football's first depth chart release
description: Vanderbilt football released its depth chart ahead of the Austin Peay season opener. Here were the five biggest surprises.
fullText:
Vanderbilt football released its first depth chart for its game against Austin Peay on Sept. 1.

As expected, the Commodores listed Blaze Berlowitz as their starting quarterback for the season opener, which is 6 p.m. CT Sept. 5 at FirstBank Stadium and will be streamed on SEC Network+.

However, freshman Jared Curtis also is expected to also play in the game.

Beyond quarterbacks, here are our biggest takeaways from the depth chart release:

Wide receiver was one of the most contested battles in the preseason after the losses of Tre Richardson and Richie Hoskins. It was known that Junior Sherrill would be one of the starters; the other two spots went to Brycen Coleman and Tristen Brown. Coleman won the job over Ja'Cory Thomas, who was one of the most frequent targets during the preseason.

Coleman has big size at 6-foot-5 and 215 pounds. He converted from tight end in the offseason.

"We love his size, first of all," Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea said. "He's always had sneaky speed. He knows how to get behind the defense and he's a smart player."

Cole Adams and Kayleb Barnett were named the other second-string receivers.

Offensive tackle was a three-way battle between Azubuike, Irving and North Dakota State transfer Beau Johnson. Clinton Azubuike and Orion Irving emerged victorious, while Johnson somewhat surprisingly will be a backup after being one of the Commodores' top transfers this offseason.

Kevo Wesley and Cade McConnell were listed as the starting guards and Lyndon Cooper as the starting center.

"Orion transferred in with a ton of snap experience a year ago," Lea said. "Served a role, we thought he was ascending last season, and really got opportunities to play for us at the position last year. We thought he played well. He's had a really good offseason. This may be one of the most improved players in our program, and maybe the strongest performer up front through training camp."

Four true freshmen cracked the depth chart, which listed two or three players at each position.

Other than Curtis, no true freshmen were on the depth chart on offense, but running back Evan Hampton was listed as one of two options as a second-string kick returner.

On defense, Mason Lewis was listed as one of two options at the hybrid linebacker/safety position, along with sophomore Carson Lawrence. Bishop Starling was listed as the third-string at one of the cornerback positions.

Miles Capers was a sure starter at one pass-rush spot, but it was a competition among several transfers for the second starting edge spot. Brian Allen Jr., who transferred from Iowa, won the job over Edwin Kolenge, a Boston College transfer.

Carson Lawrence, who was a standout in camp, also earned a starting gig, though it was listed as an "or" with Lewis.

Jordan Matthews, who transferred from Tennessee before the 2025 season and was a reserve, won the second starting corner job opposite Martel Hight.

Jaylin Lackey and Cayden Daniels were the second-string corners, while Starling and Jaylin Davies were the third-stringers.

title: Official | Borna Sosa returns to the Bundesliga via Cologne loan
description: Cologne have officially completed the signing of Croatian international Borna Sosa from Crystal Palace. The 28-year-old left-back joins the cathedral city side on loan through the end of the 2026/27 c...
fullText:
Cologne have officially completed the signing of Croatian international Borna Sosa from Crystal Palace. The 28-year-old left-back joins the cathedral city side on loan through the end of the 2026/27 campaign. No purchase option is reportedly included in the agreement. The deal concludes a deadline-day pursuit that accelerated considerably over the past 48 hours.

The defender reached a verbal agreement with Köln before the two clubs completed the remaining negotiations ahead of the deadline. Sosa joins fellow 28-year-old Gideon Mensah as another natural option on the left side and provides Cologne with considerable Bundesliga experience.

The Bundesliga remains the competition most closely associated with the strongest period of Sosa's club career. Sosa played for Stuttgart for five seasons between 2018 and 2023. At one point near the end of the 2020/21 Bundesliga campaign, Sosa even emerged as a potential German national team option after obtaining German citizenship.

Stuttgart signed the Zagreb native from Dinamo Zagreb in 2018. Following relegation during his first season, Sosa helped the Swabians immediately return to the top flight and subsequently established himself as one of the Bundesliga's most productive attacking wing-backs.

His exceptional left foot became his defining feature. Sosa supplied 35 assists and scored five goals across 115 competitive appearances for Stuttgart, repeatedly creating chances with early deliveries and crosses from advanced positions on the left.

His performances also earned him regular international recognition with Croatia and helped establish a market value that peaked at €23m. Sosa eventually left Stuttgart for Ajax in September 2023 in a deal worth approximately €8m.

What followed proved considerably less successful. The Croatian spent only one season in Amsterdam before moving to Torino on loan for the 2024/25 campaign. The Serie A side declined to exercise its purchase option, leaving Sosa to return briefly to Ajax before Crystal Palace acquired him for approximately €2.3m last summer.

Regular football again proved difficult to secure in England.

Cologne have finally supplied the route back.

Sosa's arrival gives Kwasniok a stylistically different option to Mensah. The former Stuttgart wing-back remains most comfortable when permitted to advance aggressively down the left, and his crossing quality gives Cologne another means of creating chances from wide areas. The transfer also brings considerably more experience to a Cologne squad seeking to consolidate its Bundesliga status after last season's 14th-place finish.

Sosa arrives having played Bundesliga, Eredivisie, Serie A, Premier League and European football, while also representing Croatia extensively at international level.

His first possible Bundesliga appearance back in Germany carries an additional twist.

Cologne travel to Stuttgart on Matchday 2.

"We are very pleased that Borna will strengthen us this season," Kessler said in Cologne's club statement. "He knows the Bundesliga very well from his time with VfB Stuttgart and possesses valuable international experience."

"At the same time, through our conversations we got to know him as a very reflective and positive person whose personality fits us very well and who will also contribute his experience off the pitch," Kessler continued. "With his strong left foot, his attacking drive and his high quality when crossing, he expands our possibilities and gives our game additional options."

"I know Cologne from my time in Stuttgart," Sosa himself added. "I still remember the away games very well because Cologne has one of the best atmospheres in the Bundesliga. Now I'm looking forward to experiencing that feeling as an FC player and playing here in the stadium. I've obviously followed how FC have started because I still follow the Bundesliga."

title: More detail about Elena Rybakina’s injury revealed at US Open
description: More detail has been provided for WTA World No. 2 Elena Rybakina's injury that caused her to retire from Cincinnati Open
fullText:
Tennis fans know that WTA World No. 2 Elena Rybakina is injured.

She retired from the Cincinnati Open in the middle of her match against Iga Swiatek. The issue was her foot which she was not able to push off or use to get her powerful serve motion underway.

Rybakina's team has not provided a lot of detail on the injury as she came to the US Open. She pulled out of the mixed doubles championship, which she was supposed to play with her Eisenhower Cup fellow partner and co-champ, Taylor Fritz.

MORE: 5 most memorable moments from Day 2 of 2026 US Open

Rybakina's practices last week were gentle, allowing the injury to heal.

Many thought it was an Achilles issue as they noted where her left leg was taped.

ESPN has learned that the issue is specifically with a tendon in her left heel. Rybakina feels it the most when serving as she lands on her left foot.

Her team experimented with her on trying to land the serve with the right foot, but messing with the mechanics at this point was not prudent.

MORE: 6 American women breeze into 2026 US Open Round 2 on Day 2

In her opening match against Thea Frodin, Chris McKendry and Coco Vandeweghe noted that she is not running down all of the balls. At the time, she was up a set and a break so perhaps that is a preservation move. Rybakina went on to win the match 6-3, 6-2.

Elena Rybakina, of Kazakhstan, returns to Diana Shnaider, of Russia, at the Cincinnati Open at the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason, Ohio, on Wednesday, August 19, 2026.

Rybakina is within reach of the World No. 1 ranking. She admits that is a childhood dream. There is plenty at stake for her so managing the injury over a two week time frame is a top priority.

title: Wolves adding former Thibs assistant Daniel Brady to Chris Finch's coaching staff
description: Brady is the Timberwolves' newest assistant coach.
fullText:
The Timberwolves are hiring Daniel Brady as an assistant coach, according to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.

Brady spent last season as an assistant with the Rio Grande Valley Vipers of the NBA G League. Before that, he spent three seasons as an assistant under Tom Thibodeau with the New York Knicks. As noted by Jon Krawczynski, Thibs and Chris Finch have a lot of mutual respect for one another.

Finch and Thibs have a lot of mutual respect. They speak often about the game and the job. https://t.co/8i8cEbZBzJ

Prior to his time with the Knicks, Brady spent four years with the Thunder as a player development coach and an assistant with the OKC Blue in the G League. Before that, he worked in player development and video operations with the Hawks for a few years. Brady got his start in the NBA as a video analyst with the Trail Blazers in 2012, a role he also held with the Rockets for a season.

A native of Lake Oswego, Oregon (where Kevin Love went to high school), Brady played college basketball at Northern Idaho Junior College and the University of Missouri Kansas City. His first job out of college was as a graduate manager for the University of San Diego men's basketball team, according to his LinkedIn. He also played for the Washington Generals against the Harlem Globetrotters in 2011-12.

Brady is the second newcomer to the Wolves' coaching staff this offseason, joining former Nuggets wing Will Barton, who was hired in a player development role. Minnesota lost assistants Micah Nori (Trail Blazers) and Max Lefevre (Paris Basketball) this offseason.

Pablo Prigioni, Elston Turner, Kevin Hanson, Chris Hines, and Jeff Newton are among the returning assistants on Finch's staff.
