title: Beckham and Mourinho pay tribute to Messi
description: Former England captain Sir David Beckham says Lionel Messi has inspired "millions of children worldwide," following the Argentine retiring from international football.
fullText:
Former England captain Sir David Beckham says Lionel Messi has inspired "millions of children worldwide" and his "legacy will live forever" following the Argentine's retirement from international football.

Beckham, co-owner of Messi's club Inter Miami, paid tribute to the 39-year-old's international career in which he scored 125 goals in 207 games.

Messi captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, saw them reach the final again in 2026 and won two Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024.

"This is the moment we get to look back on and realize how grateful we were to witness the greatness of a young kid with a dream," Beckham said on Instagram.

"Leo, you delivered the greatest gift to your country and, for that, your legacy will live forever. Congratulations on all you achieved for Argentina."

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho commented on Messi's retirement post on Instagram, saying "the next Copa America and the next World Cup won't be the same," without Messi involved.

Mourinho frequently managed against Messi in his first stint at Real Madrid between 2010 and 2013, a period in which the former Barcelona man won the Ballon d'Or in three consecutive years (2010-2012).

Former Argentina midfielder Angel di Maria, who also played alongside Messi at Paris St-Germain, described him as "the greatest of all time".

"All I know is that I was born in the right century to be able to witness you play, relish your performances and, on top of that, share all those years with you in the national team," he added.

Fellow Argentina World Cup winning team-mate and ex-Spurs defender Cristian Romero posted: "As a kid, I dreamed of meeting you someday. But I never imagined that life would give me the gift of sharing this with you and living by your side through the golden age and greatest era of our national team."

Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez shared a similar dream of playing with Messi "even just once," adding: "Life ended up being far more beautiful than that boy was able to imagine.

"I didn't just get to play with you, but we shared training camps, the dressing room, the conversations, the embraces, the difficult moments, the wonderful moments, and we ended up world champions together."

Fifa president Gianni Infantino said: "Congratulations on an extraordinary international career which has inspired millions and redefined the beautiful game.

"Thank you for every unforgettable memory while wearing the colors of [Argentina] and for uniting fans across every corner of the globe."

Commenting on Messi's instagram post, Argentinian Formula One driver Franco Colapinto said: "There are no words that will ever be enough to express our gratitude.

"Thank you for getting back up time and time again and giving everything to make an entire country happy. You are an example to all of us."

title: Portsmouth goalkeeper legend Knight dies aged 65
description: Goalkeeper Alan Knight, who played 801 Portsmouth games, dies aged 65 after being diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2024.
fullText:
Former Portsmouth goalkeeper Alan Knight has died aged 65 after being diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2024.

Knight spent 22 years playing at Fratton Park, making 801 appearances between 1978 and 2000 – the record for a keeper at a single English club.

Pompey fans gave him the nickname The Legend and after retiring he became both a coach and ambassador for the club.

In a moving tribute to their former player, a club statement, external said: "The word legend is often overused in football, but the fact that Alan was still known as The Legend at Pompey more than 20 years after hanging up his gloves speaks volumes.

"He will be sadly missed by the Fratton faithful, team-mates and all of us at the club who knew and loved him.

"Our thoughts are with Alan's wife Heather, his daughters Jade and Rebekah and all his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, The Legend".

Portsmouth captain Marlon Pack posted on social media: "RIP Knightsie. A true club legend who bled blue. A figure who has done so much for this football club and the wider community over so many years".

Knight kept a clean sheet on his debut, aged 16, against Rotherham in the old Division Three in 1978 and he went on to represent the club in all four divisions.

There were three promotion-winning campaigns, including a Division Three title success and Pompey's return to top-flight football for the first time in 28 years in the 1986-87 season.

Knight's final appearance for the club came aged 38 on 3 January 2000 in a 2-1 Division One defeat at Norwich, making him the only Blues player to have played across four decades.

Knight was awarded an MBE following his retirement, and was also handed the Freedom of the City of Portsmouth.

Portsmouth legend Knight reveals cancer diagnosis

'Football helped me through my cancer diagnosis'

Speaking to the BBC following his cancer diagnosis, Knight said it "came as a massive shock" but he wanted to discuss it publicly to encourage others to seek advice if they spot symptoms.

He joined a group of men playing walking football in Portsmouth and said it helped them all come to terms with their diagnoses.

"Once you get diagnosed, once the cancer word is used, it just changes everything," he said.

"The support network, having your mates around you - family first and foremost - but then to have your mates and your team-mates around you is huge.

"It gives you that lift when you can be slipping into that bit of depression."

title: Stokes to play for Adelaide Strikers in Big Bash
description: Former England captain Ben Stokes joins Adelaide Strikers for the 2026-27 season of the Big Bash League.
fullText:
Former England captain Ben Stokes has joined Adelaide Strikers for the 2026-27 season of the T20 Big Bash League.

The 35-year-old made the shock decision to retire from international cricket in June, with the announcement coming during the third and final Test of a 2-1 home series defeat against New Zealand.

Stokes played 122 Tests, 114 one-day internationals and 43 T20s for England.

He scored a superb 84 in the final against New Zealand when England dramatically won the World Cup for the first time in 2019.

"I'm really excited to be joining the Adelaide Strikers for BBL 16," said Stokes.

"I've always enjoyed playing in Australia, and when the opportunity came up to join the Strikers it was one I couldn't pass up.

"Adelaide Oval is an incredible place to play cricket, the Big Bash is a fantastic competition and the Strikers have an exciting group, so I'm looking forward to meeting the players, getting stuck in and contributing to a successful season.

"I can't wait to get started, create some special memories with the group and give Strikers fans plenty to cheer about."

Adelaide said Stokes, who had a brief stint at fellow BBL side Melbourne Renegades in 2015, would be available for the whole of the BBL 16 campaign, which starts in December.

"Ben is one of the greatest all-rounders the game has seen, a proven match-winner and a competitor who thrives under pressure," said Adelaide Strikers head coach Tim Paine, whose side start their BBL season against Sydney Thunder on 16 December.

"We're thrilled to have a player of his ability join our squad and can't wait to see him put on a show in BBL 16."

title: GB's Fery returns to Grand Slam stage - what lies ahead?
description: Shock Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery returns to the Grand Slam stage when he faces Italy's Lorenzo Musetti at the US Open.
fullText:
As the top stars congregated in New York for last year's US Open, Arthur Fery was looking in from the outside.

The Briton had just crept back inside the world's top 300 after winning an ATP Challenger event in Colombia and admits it was a "bit painful" watching players at the pinnacle of the sport.

Twelve months on, the 24-year-old is rubbing shoulders with the elite at Flushing Meadows, thanks to the stunning run to the Wimbledon semi-finals which has likely changed his life forever.

Fery's career is certainly unrecognisable compared to where it was.

He starts his US Open debut against Italian 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti on Tuesday as the 33rd-ranked player in the world, the British men's number one and a recent first-time finalist on the ATP Tour.

On watching the US Open from afar last year, Fery said: "It's a little bit painful seeing all the guys your age who you were playing with in juniors playing the US Open - and you're playing Challengers.

"You don't really want to be too stuck on other guys' results or watching matches. You want to focus on yourself.

"That's what I've been trying to do and now that I'm doing well, it's a little bit easier. You feel 

Wawrinka feels the love on Grand Slam goodbye

GB's Fearnley and Dart complete superb comeback wins

During his time as a professional, Fery has always carried himself with an air of assurance.

Although his extraordinary Wimbledon performance was unexpected, it feels he has the temperament to take the new experiences it has brought in his stride.

His debut at ATP Masters level ended in a win over Australia's James Duckworth at the Cincinnati Open, although the speed and guile of world number eight Alex de Minaur proved too much in the next round.

From there Fery travelled to North Carolina, where he finished runner-up at the ATP 250 event in Winston-Salem.

While he lost to higher-ranked Peruvian Ignacio Buse in Saturday's final, Fery says his four victories - albeit against opponents a Grand Slam semi-finalist would be expected to beat - have enhanced his sense of belonging.

"It was a very positive week for me. Obviously there is nowhere near as much attention as the Slams and big ATP events, but I've got to remind myself that its not a normal thing yet to make ATP 250 finals," Fery told BBC Sport.

"I wasn't really happy with my match in the final, but it was a long week and first time I'd played five matches in five days in a very long time.

"It's great preparation for the US Open."

Taking a month off tour after Wimbledon was another strategic move designed to help Fery flourish in the tail-end of the season.

The run scuppered an already-booked holiday to Greece, but a rearranged lads' trip to Spain - which included plenty of time on the golf course - provided the chance to recover from suddenly finding himself in the global spotlight.

"I was able to get some time off with friends and family, go on holiday and enjoy the success I'd had with them," he said.

"I'm happy with taking that amount of time off and even though I had to practise a little bit longer to get back into the flow of things, it was really worth it - mainly from a mental standpoint."

To Wimbledon and back - Fery's voyage to Centre Court spotlight

Fery narrowly missed out on a seeding at the US Open, which are given to the top 32 players, leaving him vulnerable to drawing one of the leading stars in New York.

Musetti, who is an excellent returner and slick mover, must be counted among the title favourites in a wide open men's draw.

A quarter-finalist in New York last year, the 25-year-old has gone a step further at both the French Open and Wimbledon in the recent seasons, and reached the Australian Open last eight in January.

A thigh injury ruled him out of the French Open and Wimbledon, but he has showed signs of rediscovering his best level in recent runs to the Washington and Cincinnati quarter-finals.

"Some weeks you get good draws, some weeks you get tougher draws - it is how it is," said Fery.

"I missed out by one spot on a seeded position and then I draw the 13th seed - it's a bit unfortunate but some things go your way and some things don't.

"I still feel I have my chances in that match-up if I prepare and play well."

Whatever happens against Musetti, it will be intriguing to see how Fery fares over the coming months given his new-found status.

There has already been plenty of discussion about whether the 5ft 9in Londoner's stature will be a limiting factor on an ATP Tour where taller players tend to thrive.

"I don't think Arthur's height has to be something which we sit here and worry about," says Michael Bourne, the Lawn Tennis Association's performance director.

"He has great ball speed – whether off the ground or from the serve, he's an amazing decision-maker and a very good athlete.

"He's earned the right for us not to put a ceiling on him. He's a talented young man and there is a lot to be excited about - let's see how far he can go."

title: Brighton agree £15m deal for Millwall winger Azeez
description: Brighton agree a deal to sign 25-year-old Nigeria winger Femi Azeez from Championship club Millwall.
fullText:
Brighton have agreed a deal to sign Nigeria winger Femi Azeez from Millwall.

The 25-year-old scored 11 goals and provided eight assists in 37 games last season, earning a place in the PFA Championship team of the year.

Azeez has been pushing for a move to the Premier League, with Millwall rejecting at least three bids from the Seagulls in recent weeks.

His departure would be a club record sale for Millwall, who are set to receive an initial £12.5m - potentially rising past £15m with add-ons.

Azeez would be Brighton's 11th signing of the summer, including their club record £45m move for Tottenham centre-back Luka Vuskovic.

The Seagulls have also raised significant funds through player sales, including Carlos Baleba's £70m move to Manchester United, while Liverpool have been linked with winger Yankuba Minteh.

Azeez joined Millwall from Reading for about £1m in 2024 and is entering the final two years of his contract.

He had been left out of the Lions' three most recent matchday squads by manager Alex Neil.

Fellow Championship club Wrexham are also understood to have shown an interest in Azeez.

His arrival at Brighton will allow Seagulls winger Amario Cozier-Duberry, who has signed a new contract, to leave on loan.

The 21-year-old, who had a successful loan spell at Bolton Wanderers in League One last season, is expected to join Championship side Middlesbrough this term.

He looks likely to replace Morgan Whittaker at Boro, with the winger set to join Major League Soccer side Colorado Rapids.

title: Hull sign Ansah and close on Norton-Cuffy
description: Hull City sign forward Ilyas Ansah on a five-year deal from Bundesliga side Union Berlin.
fullText:
Hull City have signed forward Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin and agreed a £12m deal for Genoa right-back Brooke Norton-Cuffy.

English full-back Cody Drameh, who has featured in all three of Hull's games this season, is heading in the opposite direction to Norton-Cuffy - with Genoa set to pay £3.4m.

Norton-Cuffy, 22, who has spent two years with the Serie A side, began his career at Arsenal and was part of the England Under-21 squad that retained the European Championship in Slovakia in 2025.

Germany Under-21 international Ansah joins Hull on a five-year contract for a reported fee of 15m euros (£12.8m) with 12m euros (£10.2m) in add-ons.

He becomes the 13th player to arrive at Hull this summer, with the club having won their first two matches since returning to the Premier League after a nine-year absence.

"I'm very excited. It's a dream come true for me to play in the Premier League, and for such a big club - it's really an honour for me," Ansah said.

"I have heard a lot about the club, the players and the team, and I'm excited to play with the boys and to get to know them.

"I'm definitely a player who always gives his best and leaves it all on the pitch."

The 6ft 4in forward, who turns 22 in November, scored five goals in 36 matches in all competitions for Union Berlin last term.

Hull also look set to sign Tim Iroegbunam after agreeing a £22m package for the Everton midfielder.

They are also in advanced talks to sign 19-year-old Olympiacos midfielder Christos Mouzakitis for about £13m.

The 11-cap Greece international progressed through Olympiacos' academy and has made 50 league appearances for the club.

title: Ski Sunday to end after nearly 50 years
description: The BBC is to end its Ski Sunday programme after nearly 50 years.
fullText:
Ski Sunday, the BBC's winter sports programme, is to end after nearly 50 years.

First broadcast in 1978, it featured the best of winter sports action, with Ed Leigh and Chemmy Alcott its most recent presenting team.

"Changing audience behaviours and the tough financial decisions needed to meet savings requirements mean BBC Sport must continually review how it delivers value for licence fee payers and serves audiences across all platforms. This decision forms part of that process," said a BBC Sport statement.

Philip Bernie, head of BBC Sport events, said Ski Sunday "has been a truly iconic programme".

He added: "Generations of viewers have enjoyed its coverage of the best in winter sports.

"We are enormously proud of the role it has played in bringing these moments to audiences across the UK, and extremely grateful to the brilliant people who have delivered them, not least the current outstanding team.

"These decisions are never easy, but as audience viewing habits evolve and we work to deliver value for licence fee payers, we have to make tough choices.

"We remain committed to bringing audiences the very best of winter sport, above all at the Winter Olympics, across BBC Sport's platforms."

title: Palace and Sunderland battling for £30m Fofana
description: Crystal Palace attempt to hijack Sunderland's move for Lyon's Malick Fofana.
fullText:
Crystal Palace are attempting to hijack Sunderland's move for Lyon's Malick Fofana.

The winger had agreed to join Sunderland in a deal worth just under £30m but Palace have made their own proposal.

It is now up to the the 21-year-old to decide as he travels to England for a medical, having been offered a five-year contract at the Stadium of Light.

Any deal for the Belgium forward would cost an initial £25.6m, with a potential £4.3m in add-ons.

Fofana was understood to be excited by the prospect of joining Sunderland before their first European campaign in 51 years, having qualified for the Europa League, but Palace have also qualified for the same competition.

Arsenal also attempted to sign Fofana, but the Premier League champions were unable to agree a fee with Lyon.

Fofana began his career at KAA Gent before joining the Ligue 1 side in 2024.

If he joins Sunderland, Fofana would sign alongside Kevin Danso, with the Austria defender due to arrive from Tottenham on an initial loan with an option to buy.

Sunderland have also signed defenders Thomas Meunier and Dayann Methalie, and midfielder Jules Ahoka, this summer after finishing seventh in their first season back in the top flight.

The Black Cats beat Fulham on Sunday after losing their opening match of the 2026-27 season at Ipswich.

title: Barcelona complete signing of Arsenal striker Jesus
description: Barcelona have completed the signing of Gabriel Jesus on a permanent deal.
fullText:
Barcelona have completed the signing of Gabriel Jesus on a permanent deal.

It comes after BBC Sport reported that a deal for the Brazilian to move to Barcelona for a fee of £8.6m (10m euros) was close to be being confirmed.

Jesus has fallen down the pecking order in recent seasons at Arsenal due to injury issues, as well as Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres being the preferred central strikers at the club.

Napoli had also shown an interest in Jesus, but the Brazilian has now joined last season's Spanish league champions after completing his medical on Monday.

Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022, scoring 32 goals and adding 22 assists in 123 appearances for the Gunners.

Speaking to the media before Arsenal's win over Aston Villa, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed that Jesus was not training with the squad.

When asked whether that meant the forward was leaving, Arteta said: "Personal situations, whatever they are, I think it's clear."

Jesus would be Barcelona's third signing from a Premier League club this summer, following the arrivals of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle and Rodri from Manchester City.

Barcelona have also been pursuing a deal for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez but Atletico have been clear of their intention to not negotiate with their La Liga rivals.

Arsenal have also been chasing Alvarez but it is unlikely that a deal is completed at this stage.

The Gunners have also sold Fabio Vieira to Hamburger SV while Ethan Nwaneri is getting closer to completing a loan move to Borussia Dortmund.

title: Newcastle sign Fernandez-Pardo from Lille for £51m
description: Newcastle United sign Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille for an initial £51.4m.
fullText:
Newcastle United have signed forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille for an initial £51.4m.

Fernandez-Pardo flew into Tyneside on Monday night to have a medical and sign a long-term contract.

The 21-year-old said he was "very proud to be at such a big club" following talks with head coach Matthias Jaissle.

"He really showed how much he wanted me to be here," the Belgium international said.

"In terms of my own career progression, it made complete sense to come so I didn't hesitate at all.

"I know the club, I know about the stadium, I know it's a fantastic atmosphere. I've followed the team.

"I'm still young, I'm still hungry, and that's why I'm here, and I want to make that progress with Newcastle. I can't wait to start the wonderful adventure here."

Fernandez-Pardo was left out of Lille's squad for the 2-2 draw against Paris St-Germain last week and ordered to train away from the first-team squad until his future was resolved.

The forward has been a long-standing target of Newcastle's - dating back to former head coach Eddie Howe's time in charge - and fits the age range the club have been targeting.

Of those players aged 21 and under across Europe's big five leagues last season, Fernandez-Pardo ranked second for big chances (21), fifth for touches in the opposition box (184) and shots on target (30), and seventh for goals and assists combined (13).

His ability to play in a number of positions across the frontline also made him an attractive target as Jaissle looked to strengthen his squad.

"Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game," Jaissle said. "He can score and assist, he has courage, and he has the ability to take players on.

"We're sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play. He has already shown in Lille that he can perform on the big stage, and we will work closely with him to keep developing his game further.

"We are excited to see him in a Newcastle United shirt."

title: Fulham agree to sign midfielders Angel and Larsson
description: Fulham agree to sign midfielders Manuel Angel and Hugo Larsson from Real Madrid and Eintracht Frankfurt respectively.
fullText:
Fulham have agreed to sign midfielders Manuel Angel and Hugo Larsson from Real Madrid and Eintracht Frankfurt respectively.

Angel, a graduate of Madrid's academy, is set to join for an undisclosed fee after making his first-team debut earlier this year.

The Spanish youth international, 22, will reunite with former boss Alvaro Arbeloa and become the third player to make the switch to Craven Cottage from the Spanish capital, following Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios.

Frankfurt's Larsson, capped 12 times by Sweden, is expected to cost €25m (£21.4m).

The 22-year-old has spent three years at the Bundesliga club, making 87 appearances in the German top flight.

Fulham have also moved into advanced talks to sign Austrian centre-back David Affengruber from Elche.

Affengruber, 25, travelled to London on Tuesday afternoon and club officials are confident of completing a deal.

If completed, Tuesday's deals would take Fulham's summer arrivals to seven, with Shea Charles and Jonah Kusi-Asare also moving to Craven Cottage.

title: McTominay to miss Scotland games with minor heart issue
description: Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay is to have a minor heart procedure after the discovery of "a mild benign arrhythmia", Napoli have announced.
fullText:
Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay is to have a minor heart procedure after the discovery of "a mild benign arrhythmia", Napoli have announced.

The 29-year-old was subsituted after 56 minutes of Sunday's 2-1 Serie A defeat by Como and will have corrective treatment "in the coming days".

Napoli expect him to return to playing after the international break in early October and McTominay himself posted on Instagram: "See you soon Napoli. I won't take long."

However, it means he is likely to miss Sebastien Pocognoli's first four games as Scotland head coach, against Slovenia (home and away), North Macedonia and Switzerland in the Nations League.

According to the NHS,, external an arrhythmia is when the heart beats too quickly or too slowly, or the heartbeat is not steady.

Napoli say McTominay will undergo cardiac arrhythmia ablation - which the British Heart Foundation explains, external is when heat or cold energy is used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

title: “Stay Out Of That” – Aaron Judge Goes Off On Red Sox Broadcaster After Incendiary Comments About Jazz Chisholm Jr. & Austin Wells
description: Will Flemming, the Red Sox play-by-play announcer for WEEI radio, faced considerable scrutiny from Yankees fans for his comments during Sunday’s series finale. Among those criticizing him were Yankees captain Aaron Judge.
fullText:
Will Flemming, the Red Sox play-by-play announcer for WEEI radio, faced considerable scrutiny from Yankees fans for his comments during Sunday's series finale. Among those criticizing him were Yankees captain Aaron Judge.

Flemming reportedly made provocative comments, suggesting that Red Sox reliever Jovani Moran intentionally hit catcher Austin Wells with a pitch. He also asked Moran to start a fight with 2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. after repeatedly criticizing Chisholm as a bush-league player and alleging that he doesn't play the game the right way.

Judge addressed some media questions ahead of the series finale against the Angels in Anaheim on Monday, where he gave a blunt take on Flemming's comments toward Wells and Chisholm Jr.

"He needs to stay out of that and not be telling people to throw at players and injure players. That's not what this game's about. That game determines home field advantage in the playoffs. It's a six-run game. They get a couple guys on and hit a big homer, all of a sudden, we're getting our bullpen guys up and in a tight spot," Judge said.

"If you're not going to hold him on, what's going on here? Are you conceding, not conceding? What's going on? It's a six-run game. It's still a close ballgame. So yeah, not too happy hearing a broadcaster is talking about trying to injure and hurt a player. He needs to clean that up," he added.

Judge has yet to resume play in the field since being sidelined with a rib injury on May 31. While reports suggest his rehab process is progressing efficiently, the Bombers could get a boost with the addition of their club captain as the season enters its final stretch before October baseball comes calling.

Speaking to the media ahead of the series opener against the Halos on Monday, Yankees skipper Aaron Boone addressed multiple game-related questions, especially their resounding series win over Boston.

Furthermore, when asked about Judge's return timeline, Boone sounded optimistic, noting his star slugger's rehab progress and the possibility that he could return as early as the next homestand.

"He's doing well. He's here, you know. He's here to kind of continue to ramp up baseball activities. So, you know, we're getting closer, but feel good about where he's at. I think it's possible. I'm not going to put a date on it, but, you know, I think those things are in play now. It's, again, about getting the durability and the workload built up on him, which is the biggest thing now," Boone said.

The Yankees lost Monday's series opener to the Angels, 10-1, and will aim to bounce back in Game 2 on Tuesday night to avoid a series defeat.

After Los Angeles, the Bombers will travel to San Diego for a three-game series against the Padres, then head back to the Bronx to begin a six-game homestand against the Rockies and the Mets.

title: What kind of player is Balogun?
description: Everton have agreed a £40m deal to sign USA international Folarin Balogun from Monaco, with a medical set to take place on Tuesday.  A one-time Arsenal academy graduate, Balogun joined Monaco from the Gunners for £35m in 2023, going on to score 31 goals in 91 appearances for the Ligue 1 club.  Whereas Barry is more of a target man adept at winning balls in the air, Balogun boasts greater pace and a game built around making runs behind opposition defences.
fullText:
Everton have agreed a £40m deal to sign USA international Folarin Balogun from Monaco, with a medical set to take place on Tuesday.

So what type of player will the Blues be signing and how does he compare with Thierno Barry, the Toffees' current first-choice striker?

A one-time Arsenal academy graduate, Balogun joined Monaco from the Gunners for £35m in 2023, going on to score 31 goals in 91 appearances for the Ligue 1 club.

He missed four months of the 2024-25 campaign due to injury but after returning to fitness in April he enjoyed the most prolific season of his career to date in 2025-26, scoring 19 goals in 43 games, including five in the Champions League.

Whereas Barry is more of a target man adept at winning balls in the air, Balogun boasts greater pace and a game built around making runs behind opposition defences.

At the World Cup earlier this summer, the 25-year-old averaged eight runs in behind per game, ranking him third of all strikers, and scored three goals.

His goals-per-minute ratio was almost identical to that of Beto, who is leaving Everton for Fiorentina in a £15m deal, in league football last season.

But Balogun's younger age and Champions League experience suggest his ceiling could be comparatively higher.

His tally of 19 goals last season is at least seven more than either Beto or Barry have managed in a campaign with a club in an elite European league.

title: Why Katie Taylor’s final fight at Croke Park is not about what happens in the ring
description: An Irish icon, Olympic gold medalist, and undisputed champion at two weights, Taylor finally realises her Croke Park dream this weekend – as she says farewell to boxing
fullText:
It took minutes to convince everybody that Katie Taylor truly did deserve a final fight in front of 80,000 people at Croke Park in Dublin on Saturday night.

The tickets went on sale and then the tickets for boxing's greatest final fight sold out; it was all over in 30 minutes of trading, and Taylor's position as one of the most popular fighters in history was secure.

The journey to the very end of the boxing line started so long ago when Taylor, with her hair in braids tucked inside a headguard, posed as a boy to have her first fight. A legend was born on a tiny amateur show, and the girl from Bray was on her way.

The battle for equality was on; Taylor moved through the ranks, became the star of the Irish boxing team, won medals in tournaments all over the world and then won the Olympic title in London in 2012.

At Dublin airport there are three giant pictures of iconic people arriving in the Irish capital; there is the pope, there is a smiling President John F Kennedy, and the final picture is a joyous shot of Taylor with her gold medal in her hand, smiling from the cockpit of a plane.

The hero was back from London that afternoon in the summer of 2012, and this Saturday that long road to glory will finish at the home of Irish sport. The sacred ground will belong to the small girl from Bray – it has been a dream all her boxing life.

Flora Pili, an unbeaten Frenchwoman, was picked for the final dance in the ring. The fight is for three versions of the super-lightweight title, but at this point in her remarkable career, all glittering baubles are an unnecessary distraction. Taylor has won so many and in so many fights; her ring genius is not measured by the amount of costume belts that can be strapped across her body.

Taylor is now 40 and this last fight will be her 21st consecutive world-title fight, a run that started in 2017; there was the one loss against Chantelle Cameron in Dublin 2023 and then the triumphant rematch victory a few months later.

She has dominated and led the revolution from the ground up; she was once the little girl pretending to be a boy to get a fight, and on Saturday she will be the multi-millionaire national hero walking to the ring on a bed of love and adoration to thank the faithful. It's a boxing fairytale, make no mistake.

For Saturday's fight, Taylor had the pick of any woman operating within a 10lb range of the 140lb limit, and there were dozens waiting for the call. In the end, it was Pili, fresh, unbeaten, and a safe choice for a fight and night when the opponent's credentials are irrelevant. Pili can make it difficult if Taylor is overwhelmed by emotion and the vastness of the event.

However, this is not about Taylor having one final test, one final great victory – it is all about the walk to the ring and saying goodbye, and 80,000 people howling and smiling and crying. There has never been a final fight in boxing history quite like this. A nation will stop for the tiny girl from Bray one last time.

title: ‘I’d Give Him a Quick Little $5,000’ — Hall of Famer Wants Quick Resolution on Odell Beckham Jr.’s Giants Roadblock
description: Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has officially returned to the New York Giants, in what is shaping up to be an exciting moment for fans who were reminiscing about his impact during his first stint with the franchise.
fullText:
Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has officially returned to the New York Giants, in what is shaping up to be an exciting moment for fans who were reminiscing about his impact during his first stint with the franchise. As he is now back on the Giants' 53-man roster, Beckham has another goal in mind: reclaiming his iconic No. 13 jersey.

That, however, may need some doing, considering Jalin Hyatt currently has his hands on the number. However, Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe knows how Beckham can get his jersey number back.

Hyatt has worn No. 13 for the New York Giants over the past few seasons. However, he was recently waived by the team before being brought back to the practice squad.

That situation could make the jersey-number discussion much easier for Beckham. Since Hyatt is no longer part of the Giants' 53-man roster, the two could potentially settle the matter with a simple discussion.

Hyatt's production also doesn't quite match what Beckham accomplished while wearing No. 13 in New York. That could give Beckham another argument for reclaiming the jersey that became synonymous with him during his first stint with the Giants.

The topic came up during the latest episode of the"Nightcap" podcast. Co-host Chad Johnson suggested that practice-squad players should be willing to give up a jersey number when a former star associated with that number returns to the team.

Johnson explained that seeing #13 on a Giants uniform immediately reminds him of Beckham and everything the receiver accomplished during his first few seasons in the NFL.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

Meanwhile, Sharpe offered a straightforward solution to OBJ's problem.

"I would give him (Hyatt) a quick little $5,000," Sharpe said.

When Johnson jokingly argued that Hyatt shouldn't be disrespected during the jersey-number debate, Sharpe fired back with an amusing response.

"He disrespected my jersey by getting it," Sharpe said. "You know you ain't supposed to get that jersey like that after what I did there the first 3-4 years of my career."

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Beckham wore No. 3 during the preseason, but that number belongs to linebacker Abdul Carter. Beckham has already made it clear that his preference is to return to No. 13.

"I think we all know what that means to me," Beckham told reporters on Monday. "There definitely will be some conversations. I'll just say we'll see what happens. But, like I said, it would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on."

There is little doubt that No. 13 carries significant meaning for both Beckham and Giants fans. New York selected Beckham 12th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft, and he quickly established himself as one of the most electrifying wide receivers of his generation.

Beckham never won a Super Bowl with the Giants, but his first stint in New York was filled with individual accomplishments. He won Offensive Rookie of the Year and was named to three Pro Bowls.

title: Barcelona new signing compares La Liga with the Premier League – ‘Football here is different’
description: Anthony Gordon produced a stellar performance in the final third as Barcelona secured a comprehensive 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night.The summer signing from Newcastle United notably assis...
fullText:
Anthony Gordon produced a stellar performance in the final third as Barcelona secured a comprehensive 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night.

The summer signing from Newcastle United notably assisted one of the goals from Raphinha while also playing a crucial role in Florian Lejeune's own goal.

The Englishman demonstrated excellent chemistry with his teammates and appears to be settling in well in La Liga.

In the wake of his performance against Rayo, the forward tried to compare La Liga's brand of football with the Premier League.

Gordon acknowledged the intensity of English football but highlighted the different demands of Spanish football.

"I'm not going to deny that the Premier League is incredibly intense. The rhythm is relentless, there are physical battles everywhere, long band kicks, corner kicks and a lot of contact.

Gordon had an outstanding game vs Rayo. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"That's why many English players believe it is the best league in the world. They're used to that kind of chaos," he said, as quoted by SPORT.

The Englishman then pointed out the nuances of Spanish football, especially in relation to the recent game against Rayo Vallecano.

"Football in Spain is different. Rayo retreated and tried to make the match difficult, something you also see in many mid-table Premier League teams. The difference is that we don't just resort to long balls or relying on ball-to-ball plays," he said.

Gordon praised Barcelona's style as the key differentiator, saying: "We moved the ball, Pedri found spaces between the lines, Lamine and the others created numerical superiority and patiently disarmed them with our football."

The forward also flagged the technical precision required in La Liga, as he said:

"In England, sometimes intensity can cover up mistakes. You can mis-control the ball and still recover by winning the next physical battle. Here, a bad first touch or a lack of concentration on your positioning can punish you immediately."

"The spaces are smaller, the decisions have to be faster and everything must be cleaner," he added.

Gordon's cross forced Lejeune's own goal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Gordon believes the Spanish game actually enhances one of his biggest strengths.

"My speed becomes even more effective here because the movement around me creates opportunities and spaces, rather than everyone simply running forward in straight lines," he said.

At the same time, though, the Englishman was careful not to disrespect the league in which he grew up.

"I loved playing in the Premier League and it played a huge role in my development. But Spanish football demands a different level of tactical and technical intelligence," he said.

He did, however, offer an observation about how certain English sides would cope.

"Some Premier League teams would have a hard time playing this style consistently because they may not have the patience or quality in the midfield that is required."

"That's not disrespecting them, it's just what I've noticed in my first games. There's a different football intelligence here," Gordon concluded.

title: Serie A 2026/27: Inter Milan make a strong start to their title defence
description: The start of the 2026/27 Serie A season has generated plenty of talking points, particularly for the clubs with title aspirations.Six teams have an unblemished record after two games and four of them ...
fullText:
The start of the 2026/27 Serie A season has generated plenty of talking points, particularly for the clubs with title aspirations.

Six teams have an unblemished record after two games and four of them are teams who are expected to be battling to win the Scudetto this term.

Without further ado, read on as we look at how the Serie A title race is taking shape, starting with defending champions Inter Milan.

After recording an impressive 4-1 home victory over Monza in their opening game, Inter were made to work a little harder in their second outing at Cagliari.

Hakan Calhanoglu's long-range strike settled the game, but Cristian Chivu's side needed two decisive saves from Josep Martinez to seal the win.

Calhanoglu is now the only midfielder to have scored more than once in each of the last 14 seasons across Europe's top five leagues, highlighting his importance to the team.

However, Martinez arguably stole the show, making a pair of excellent stops in the second half to keep the home side at bay.

Yann Bisseck also stepped up when it mattered, heading a goal-bound effort over the bar as Cagliari desperately fought to equalise.

Inter's ability to sig deep when they are under pressure is an attribute which should serve them extremely well as the season progresses.

A pair of hugely impressive 4-0 victories over Fiorentina and Lecce in their first two fixtures have fired Roma to the top of the Serie A standings.

Donyell Malen has been a standout performer, scoring five goals in two games. He has now bagged 19 goals in 20 league appearances since joining the club from Aston Villa.

Having guided Roma to third place in Serie A last season, manager Gian Piero Gasperini is eager to knock Inter off their perch this time around.

Gasperini's team are entertaining to watch when they are in full flow, but it is too early to determine whether they are genuine title contenders.

The upcoming home game against Atalanta will provide a useful indicator of their title hopes. They are also scheduled to host Inter Milan this month.

If Roma can reach the international break with their unbeaten record intact, it would be impossible to dismiss their chances of winning the Scudetto.

Former Manchester United Ruben Amorim has made a solid start to life in Serie A by guiding AC Milan to victories over Torino and Venezia.

However, it would be fair to categorise Milan as 'a work in progress' and it will be intriguing to see how they fare when they face one of the top teams.

Striker Goncalo Ramos got off the mark for the season against Venezia, but he will need to be more clinical if Milan are to mount a sustained title challenge.

His wastefulness in front of goal kept Venezia in the game, and Amorim will be concerned by how often they breached Milan's defence.

Visits to Juventus and Lazio in their next two games will demonstrate whether Milan have what it takes to stay in the title race this season.

Intriguingly, Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira have yet to feature this term, so the level of performances could increase when they are integrated into the team.

Juventus have been steady rather than spectacular in their first two games, defeating Frosinone and Parma without conceding a goal.

Luciano ​Spalletti's side wasted plenty of decent opportunities against Parma, but eventually got the job done courtesy of Teun Koopmeiners late effort.

After buying extremely well during the summer transfer window, Juventus look well-placed to mount a sustained title challenge this season.

Atalanta and Lazio are the only other Serie A teams with a 100 percent record after two games, but neither appeal as potential Scudetto winners.

La Dea were extremely fortunate to beat Bologna in their second outing, while Lazio's lack of firepower is still a major issue.

Napoli suffered a defeat in their second outing against Como, but should be capable of forcing their way into contention over the coming weeks.

Inter were worthy champions last season and they will be a tough nut to crack this time around.

Roma could keep themselves in contention under Gasperini, but Milan may be the biggest threat to the defending champions this term.

title: Lyon winger Fofana set for £30m Sunderland move
description: Sunderland agree a deal worth just under £30m for Lyon winger Malick Fofana, who is set to sign a five-year contract.
fullText:
Sunderland have agreed a deal worth just under £30m for Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

The 21-year-old is travelling to England for a medical and is expected to sign a five-year contract.

The deal for the Belgium forward will cost an initial £25.6m, with a potential £4.3m in add-ons.

Fofana is understood to be excited by the prospect of joining Sunderland before their first European campaign in 51 years, having qualified for the Europa League.

The move follows attempts by Arsenal to sign Fofana, but the Premier League champions were unable to agree a fee with Lyon.

Fofana began his career at KAA Gent before joining the Ligue 1 side in 2024.

He is set to join Kevin Danso at Sunderland, with the Austria defender due to arrive from Tottenham on an initial loan with an option to buy.

Sunderland have also signed defenders Thomas Meunier and Dayann Methalie, and midfielder Jules Ahoka, this summer after finishing seventh in their first season back in the top flight.

title: Drama continues in Pakistan cricket: Misbah-ul-Haq resigns from PCB selection committee after 7 players were sent home from England tour
description: Misbah-ul-Haq has resigned from the PCB selection committee after reportedly being bypassed over the decision to send 7 players home from the England Test tour.
fullText:
Drama continues in Pakistan cricket: Misbah-ul-Haq resigns from PCB selection committee after 7 players were sent home from England tour originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Misbah-ul-Haq has reportedly stepped down from the PCB's selection committee.

Misbah's decision comes a day after Pakistan sent back seven players from their Test squad in the middle of the England series.

Misbah was reportedly unhappy with the decision to make changes in the squad in the middle of a series.

Misbah-ul-Haq has walked away from his role on the PCB selection committee after seven Test players were abruptly pulled out of the England tour following the 194-run defeat at Lord's.

According to The Express Tribune, Misbah has already submitted his resignation letter to the board. He's expected to work through a notice period before officially stepping away from the role.

What seems to have triggered this was the PCB's decision to release seven players from the squad following the crushing loss at Lord's, bringing in fresh faces for the series finale at Edgbaston instead.

MORE: Has any team made drastic changes to their squad in the middle of a series before?

Misbah, despite sitting on the selection committee, was reportedly left completely out of the loop on how and why those calls were made, and that exclusion clearly didn't sit well with him.

Moreover, Sarfaraz Ahmed lost his job as red-ball head coach, and Umar Gul was also relieved of his fast-bowling coach duties. White-ball head coach Mike Hesson, alongside bowling coach Ashley Noffke, have been asked to step in to steady things for the Edgbaston Test as the board didn't have many options left with the series on the line.

MORE: Five times Pakistan shocked the cricket world: Instances when PCB took weird calls

Misbah's association with the panel only goes back to March 2026, when the PCB revamped the committee after Aleem Dar stepped down following a rough T20 World Cup campaign. Sarfaraz had joined the selection setup around the same time, before later taking the red-ball coaching job on April 18.

It was just ahead of a two-Test tour of Bangladesh that Pakistan lost 2-0. A subsequent series against West Indies ended in a 1-1 draw, hardly the platform of stability the team needed heading into England.

Now, with Pakistan 2-0 down and facing a series whitewash at Edgbaston, the mounting results pressure appears to have finally cracked the working relationships behind the scenes.

MORE: Pakistan's head coach and captain merry-go-round: Are the players scapegoats?

Misbah's resignation isn't really surprising once you look at the pattern here. Pakistan cricket has a long, tiring habit of making major calls without proper consultation, then acting shocked when senior figures walk out the door.

When you sideline a sitting selector from such an important decision as sending seven players home mid-series isn't just poor etiquette; it's a structural failure. You can't build a functioning selection process if half the committee finds out about major moves after they've already happened.

MORE: 'T20 players included for Tests': Afridi, Malik blasts PAK selectors over squad selection

This kind of chaos doesn't just cost Pakistan on the field, though that's bad enough with a whitewash now looming. It corrodes trust among the very people meant to steer the team through rough patches. Until PCB fixes how decisions actually get made, rather than just reshuffling names in and out of jobs, these resignations and walkouts are only going to keep piling up.

title: Giants' Malik Nabers 'feels good,' but won't commit to Week 1 return
description: New York Giants WR Malik Nabers says he feels good, even "real good," but won't commit to playing in Week 1.
fullText:
One of the big questions surrounding the New York Giants this summer is whether their No. 1 wide receiver, Malik Nabers, will be ready for the regular season.

With 12 days until the Giants' opener against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football at MetLife Stadium, the question remains unanswered.

Nabers tore his ACL and meniscus last October and had a complicated rehab after surgery. He then needed a second surgery this spring to "clean up" scar tissue.

Nabers told reporters on Monday that he's not sure if he'll play in the opener, but he's doing everything he can to get ready.

"My mind is focused on playing the regular season, playing whenever that is and playing what team it is," he said. "I'm going to be making sure that I'm ready to go out there and I'm healthy enough to play all four quarters. That nobody got to make sure I'm not in on every play, or they have to make sure I got enough snaps or my snaps are limited. So, that's the main focus is just trying to be out there as much as I can."

The decision is not all Nabers' to make. The Giants' medical and training staff have to sign off on his return to 100 percent participation.

"I feel pretty good. Well, I feel real good, to be honest. But like I said, you're going to feel good, but there's still some things that you still have to check off the box for you to participate," said Nabers. "So, I'm still going through that, still listening to the trainers, still listening to doctors and sharing everything with them."

What checkpoints was he speaking of?

"I'm going to keep the checkpoints in-house. It's not really anything too big, but as I said, I'm going to keep it more in-house and just to myself."

Both are rookies who have stood out in their respective training camps. Eason especially as a member of the San Francisco 49ers.

Kansas City Chiefs part ways with a preseason standout to take advantage of another NFL team's mistake | A to Z Sports

Locked on 49ers host Brian Peacock had this to say:

"Bryson Eason is a tough one for the 49ers to lose. He showed enough promise as an undrafted rookie, outplayed some guys on the roster, and looked more valuable long term than some other bubble players that were kept (likely due to draft status)."

So, Kansas City is essentially swapping a standout of their own for a standout in San Francisco. If Harris isn't claimed on waivers, the Chiefs can always bring him back on the practice squad. Either way, Eason's fit also plays a big role here.

Kansas City Chiefs spoil Lane Kiffin, LSU football's plan of adding NFL linebacker | Yahoo! Sports

However, his spot on Kansas City's 53-man roster likely ends his SEC return plans. The Chiefs also claimed defensive tackle Bryson Eason after San Francisco released him Sunday.

Kiffin has openly defended LSU's decision to pursue players caught between college and professional football. "At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they're either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country," Kiffin said earlier.

Chiefs add 12 players to initial practice squad. Here's what you need to know | The Kansas City Star

At 6-foot-3 and 346 pounds, Brevard will be a developmental nose tackle for the Chiefs. Brevard's college football experience was unique, with time spent at Penn State (2020-21), Purdue (2022-24) and Texas (2025). In 2024, Brevard earned honorable mention All-Big Ten recognition with 19 tackles, including 5.5 for loss and 1.5 sacks.

Chiefs' Failed Offseason Signing Lands With Division Rival Chargers | Heavy Sports

The Chiefs acquired Elam this past spring. It was a typical signing for Veach, who loves to take flyers on former high draft picks who haven't panned out for other teams. Elam was selected No. 23 overall by the Buffalo Bills in the 2022 NFL Draft. Ironically, the Bills only took Elam because the Chiefs traded up over them to select Trent McDuffie, who Buffalo was hoping to land.

Kansas City was hoping to unlock the talent that made Elam a high draft pick, but it didn't work out. The cornerback room quickly became crowded with young talent, and Elam wasn't able to separate himself from the pack. The Chargers will be Elam's fourth team in three years after spending time with the Chiefs, Bills, and Dallas Cowboys.

New Chiefs joint real estate venture to develop mixed-use districts in KCK and Olathe | KCTV 5

The Kansas City Chiefs and Hunt Midwest are launching a joint real estate venture called Two-Point Development as they work toward mixed-use districts in both Kansas City, Kansas, and Olathe.

The Chiefs announced Monday that the newly-formed company will help shape "vibrant, mixed-use districts around the franchise's new stadium in Kansas City, Kansas, and new headquarters and training facility in Olathe, Kansas."

Cowboys waive QB Joe Milton, clearing way for Sam Howell to be backup | The Athletic

In a surprising move, the Dallas Cowboys waived backup quarterback Joe Milton on Monday, a day after he was on the team's initial 53-man roster. He struggled a bit in Dallas' final preseason game Friday after he was outstanding in the first two, but Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said the backup battle between Milton and Sam Howell was "neck-and-neck."

Rams' Aaron Donald misses practice as planned; return date TBD | ESPN

Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald did not practice Monday, something coach Sean McVay said "was part of the plan all along."

McVay reiterated that he didn't want to put a timeline on when Donald will play his first game after being retired for two years. But he did not rule out Donald not traveling to Melbourne, Australia, to play in the Rams' season opener against the San Francisco 49ers on Sept. 10.

"Oh, yeah, absolutely," McVay said when asked whether there was a scenario Donald doesn't play in Week 1. "That could be a possibility. I wouldn't rule anything out yet.

Undrafted Rookie Jalon Daniels earns Bucs QB2 gig behind Baker Mayfield | NFL.com

With a strong training camp and preseason, Daniels leapfrogged Jake Browning and Connor Bazelak for the No. 2 QB gig behind Baker Mayfield.

"I'm proud of Jalon," Mayfield said from his charitable event at Topgolf on Sunday, via the Tampa Bay Times. "I think he's shown tremendous steps from the first time I met him in the offseason until now. He played his tail off. Worked hard. Worked on the things the coaches wanted to get done out of him and for him to progress with."

Chiefs Preseason Week 3 snap count analysis

Over 13 pass-play snaps against Seattle, rookie wideout Cyrus Allen aligned in the slot 100% of the time, according to Pro Football Focus.

He caught just one of the two passes thrown to him, but the usage of Allen in the slot is a continuation of a trend from his time at the University of Cincinnati. In 2025, Allen was in the slot for over 90% of the pass plays in the Bearcats' offense.

In camp, Allen has shown a more well-rounded skill set, but in his rookie year, the offense may focus on using the preseason standout where he is most comfortable and experienced while he develops long-term.

title: Where is the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster’s biggest weakness?
description: Scanning the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster for their biggest needs and weaknesses.
fullText:
Forming a 53-man roster is a never-ending business in the NFL. The Detroit Lions may have settled on an initial 53-man roster and 15 of their 16 practice squad players, but general manager Brad Holmes and the rest of the Lions' personnel department are not "finished."

The job of an NFL personnel employee is never done. The search for upgrades at every position continues throughout the entire season. Whether it's free agency, the waiver wire, the NFL Draft, the trade deadline, or any other time of year, there is a humongous pool of football talent available, and opportunities abound.

That job never ends, because no NFL roster is perfect. There are holes, depth issues, injury insurance needed, and new players who just don't end up working out. The Detroit Lions are no exception to this.

You better believe that this week the Lions will continue to look across the NFL landscape and hundreds of newly available players and see if they can upgrade their team. But before they do that, they need to evaluate the status of their own roster. So today's Question of the Day is:

My answer: I think my answer is the same it was when the Lions entered training camp: cornerback.

While I've certainly been encouraged by the play of starters D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin thus far, I haven't had that same level of optimism with the depth. Ennis Rakestraw had a very up-and-down camp with more downs than ups. Roger McCreary, who I believed to be a savvy pickup, has had flashes (particularly in the first two preseason games), but has underwhelmed from my previous expectations. The most promising player amongst the depth is Nick Whiteside, and Detroit didn't even believe he played well enough to warrant a spot on the 53-man roster, risking losing him by putting him on waivers before bringing him back to the practice squad.

The situation at nickel may be even more dire. While things were trending toward Christian Izien winning the starting job before his injury, that felt more like no one winning the job than anything. McCreary didn't stand out. Rakestraw was kept on the outside. And rookie Keith Abney is clearly still adjusting to being a full-time nickel after having more success on the outside in college. Not only do I not know who the starter at nickel will be in Week 1, I'm not sure who the best possible reserve is, either.

I say all of this not to induce panic. I'm actually a pretty big fan of the rest of this roster, and if the Lions can get plenty of healthy playing time out of Reed and Ya-Sin, maybe they'll hold up at cornerback, too.

But if I were Holmes and company, I'd certainly keep my ears and eyes open to upgrading the cornerback room.

title: Phillies Offer Frustrating 3-Word Update On Stymied Shortstop Aidan Miller
description: Philadelphia Phillies’ executive Dave Dombrowski sent a brief message about the top prospect following an unfortunate injury setback.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies have already received meaningful contributions from some of their top prospects this season, with Justin Crawford and Andrew Painter making the jump to the major leagues and earning lasting roles as the team tries to earn another National League East title this season.

With a top-heavy farm system, the Phillies don't have much exciting prospect depth, but both players were seen as very likely to make their debuts this year after strong minor league campaigns in 2025.

"Painter was a lock to make the team with Zack Wheeler recovering from thoracic outlet decompression surgery," Todd Zolecki wrote for MLB.com. "Crawford was a lock with the organization parting ways with center fielder Harrison Bader."

Another highly regarded prospect who once seemed to be a lock for promotion this year has instead watched his season disappear before it ever really began.

Red Sox Owner Makes Conspicuous Change In Tumultuous Season

Phillies top prospect Aidan Miller has been sidelined by a persistent back problem, leaving fans frustrated as they wait to see what the prized infielder can do at the upper levels of the organization.

In early June, the team announced a concerning setback for the young shortstop which further delayed his ability to make any progress toward a debut. He was diagnosed with discogenic pain and facet inflammation in his lumbar spine, requiring a procedure and significant recovery. At the time, the team indicated he would be able to return to game activity in six to eight weeks.

"The infielder has not played in a game this year," NBC Sports Philadelphia's Cole Weintraub noted at the time of that announcement. "The back issue kept him out of Grapefruit League action and delayed what was expected to be his first full season at Triple-A."

With that procedure scheduled to take place more than two months ago, it would seem that the team might have a more promising update to share with fans on Miller's progress. But that doesn't seem to be the case.

Yankees World Series Infielder Sends Retirement Message, 'Coolest Memory'

The latest update from Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski offered little clarity on when Miller might get back onto a diamond.

"Continuing to progress," Dombrowski said late last week Friday when asked about the top ranked prospect, according to The Athletic's Matt Gelb and Charlotte Varnes.

That three-word response might be encouraging on the surface, as progress is important, but it also suggests Miller is not all that close to playing in meaningful games.

While Crawford has provided the Phillies with another athletic option in the outfield and Painter has managed to recover from a slow start to eat some significant innings, Miller was supposed to be part of that next wave, too.

Instead, his development still appears to be stuck in a holding pattern according to the latest update likely to frustrate fans.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s World Cup records compared as international rivalry ends
description: Lionel Messi has now confirmed that he has retired from the international football stage. The Inter Miami forward made the announcement this week, meaning his final appearance for his country came at the 2026 World Cup earlier this summer.
fullText:
Lionel Messi has now confirmed that he has retired from the international football stage.

The Inter Miami forward made the announcement this week, meaning his final appearance for his country came at the 2026 World Cup earlier this summer.

Argentina made it to the final for the second tournament in a row, but unlike in 2022, the South American side were bested in the final, losing 1-0 to Spain.

Still, Messi had a great individual tournament and posted some impressive numbers. But how does he compare to Cristiano Ronaldo on the grandest stage?

Messi and Ronaldo have long been viewed as two of the best, if not the best, players in the history of football.

Their rivalry has been legendary, constantly fighting for league titles in Spain, competing for the Champions League and often going head-to-head in the Ballon d'Or race.

But when it comes to the World Cup, it is clear that Messi has outperformed CR7 over the years.

Both have competed at six tournaments, making their debuts at the 2006 World Cup.

20 years on, Messi has played 34 games in the competition for a total of 3,054 minutes compared to 27 appearances and 2,150 minutes for Ronaldo.

In those matches, the Argentine has scored 21 and provided 12 assists, while Ronaldo has 11 goals and two assists.

Messi (7) also has more goals in the knockout phase of the World Cup than Ronaldo, who had to wait until 2026 to score his first and only goal in the latter stages of the competition (vs Croatia).

title: ‘The league’s a disaster right now’: Mike Francesa calls out WNBA
description: It’s been a wild summer for the WNBA, between the seemingly endless controversies involving Caitlin Clark and all of the political firestorm that ensued after Sophie Cunningham spoke out against transgender women in women’s sports. While it’s certainly led to a lot of media attention, it isn’t exactly good attention. Over the past few months,…
fullText:
It's been a wild summer for the WNBA, between the seemingly endless controversies involving Caitlin Clark and all of the political firestorm that ensued after Sophie Cunningham spoke out against transgender women in women's sports. While it's certainly led to a lot of media attention, it isn't exactly good attention.

Over the past few months, the WNBA has become the most toxic space in all sports as players and the league itself have become political pawns. Now, longtime radio host Mike Francesa is calling out the league's leadership.

During his podcast this week, Mike Francesa was asked his take on the current state of the WNBA, and he was certainly not shy about blaming the WNBA's leadership for not having the foresight to see how things would change once Clark entered the league and the players for not welcoming her.

"They have turned their league into a bubbling, volcanic, political, chaotic situation where every nut is now getting involved politically in the WNBA on all different levels," Francesa ranted on his podcast. "It's the worst thing that could have ever happened. I blame the people who run the league, I blame the players who didn't have the long-range vision and didn't have the smarts to realize what Caitlin Clark was going to do for their league, and instead, tried to hurt her and run her out of the league at every point."

Francesa went on to compare Clark to when Pete Maravich joined the Atlanta Hawks.

"There were revolts against Pete Maravich when he came to the NBA," Francesa recalled. "He broke up a very good Atlanta Hawks team because there was insane jealousy and people felt he hadn't earned anything and they felt he was just a self-promoting showboat."

While the issues might have started with Clark, Francesa acknowledges that the issues are far beyond her at this point.

"Caitlin Clark came to that league and energized it in a way that they had never seen possible," Francesa added.  "They had never been able to sell that league to anybody, and she sold it to everybody. And they're all trying to ruin it. And now it's become a political mess way past just the issues with Caitlin Clark. The league's a disaster right now."

The post 'The league's a disaster right now': Mike Francesa calls out WNBA appeared first on The Comeback: Today's Top Sports Stories & Reactions.

title: Scottie Scheffler sets new PGA Tour record by achieving feat no other player in history has managed
description: Scottie Scheffler finished his 2026 PGA Tour season in style on Sunday at East Lake. Scheffler won the Tour Championship by three strokes after shooting a final-round 66, and he secured his second FedEx Cup trophy in the process.
fullText:
Scottie Scheffler finished his 2026 PGA Tour season in style on Sunday at East Lake.

Scheffler won the Tour Championship by three strokes after shooting a final-round 66, and he secured his second FedEx Cup trophy in the process.

The 30-year-old world number one ended the PGA Tour season with three wins.

While that represents somewhat of a drop-off for Scottie Scheffler, his numbers are actually even better than last season.

He recorded the lowest ever scoring average in PGA Tour history this season.

Meanwhile, Scheffler is now fifth on the all-time PGA Tour win percentage list, behind only Tiger Woods, Ben Hogan, Byron Nelson and Sam Snead.

At the Tour Championship on Sunday, though, Scheffler achieved a feat that no other player in history has managed.

It's fair to argue that Scheffler is already one of the greatest golfers in the history of the sport.

In order to become one of the best four or five golfers of all-time, though, he will need to continue doing what he's doing for the next 5-10 years.

That said, he has already broken two PGA Tour records.

However, one of them is far more meaningful than the other.

Scheffler became the career money leader on the PGA Tour on Sunday, but that one doesn't hold that much weight, considering the recent purse increases.

However, another record that he has now broken does have genuine meaning.

Scheffler's win at the Tour Championship on Sunday saw him top the money list for the fifth consecutive season.

Even Tiger Woods or Jack Nicklaus were unable to manage that.

Topping the PGA Tour money list for five consecutive seasons is a record that Scottie Scheffler can be truly proud of.

It is evidence of his remarkably consistent brilliance.

The worrying thing for his rivals is that he doesn't seem to be slowing down either.

There's a good chance that in 10 years' time, we will be talking about Scottie Scheffler as one of the genuine greats of the game.

The world number one just needs to remain hungry to keep getting better and there is no doubt that he will end up compiling one of the most successful PGA Tour careers of all time.

title: ‘He’s a joke’ – Frustrated Mariners fans send clear message to Julio Rodriguez after Red Sox gaffe
description: The Seattle Mariners sank to a new low on Monday evening in their loss against the Boston Red Sox. Julio Rodriguez was the man under scrutiny as Dan Wilson’s team capitulated at Fenway Park, as they lost the game after ten innings.
fullText:
The Seattle Mariners sank to a new low on Monday evening in their loss against the Boston Red Sox.

Julio Rodriguez was the man under scrutiny as Dan Wilson's team capitulated at Fenway Park, as they lost the game after ten innings.

The Mariners held a three-run lead heading into the eighth, but errors cost them once again, with the Red Sox scoring four runs across the eighth, ninth and tenth innings.

An opportunity for the sensational turnaround was provided by Rodriguez failing to secure a Roman Anthony hit, which allowed the Red Sox to level the score.

After making a strong postseason run last year, the Mariners have looked like a total shadow of the team that played last season.

Fans have clearly grown tired of their poor form and Rodriguez faced the backlash on Monday.

It has been a season to forget for the Mariners as they currently sit 64-74 ahead of the remaining weeks of the 2026 season.

Rodriguez is a player who the fans would hope to depend on, but he really let the side down on Monday evening.

'Dude acts like he is younger than he is.. needs to grow up,' said one Mariners fan on X.

'They should remove the no fly zone from T Mobile and replace it with a bozo the clown banner,' replied another.

Rodriguez has hit 20 home runs this season for the Mariners, but his usual dependability in the outfield has now come under real scrutiny.

One extremely frustrated fan even said: 'Biggest disappointment in Mariners history. He'll never get it.'

'Steady decline since his rookie season in just about every category…' said another.

Rodriguez signed a 13-year contract with the Mariners through until 2035, which guarantees him $210m, and could even reach a huge $470m.

Frustrations were high among Mariners fans: 'Complacency set in. He thought he was the greatest thing since sliced bread.'

'Bench him. He's a joke,' one fan even said.

The time has come: in just four days, the 2026-27 Ohio State football Buckeyes will take to the field for the first official time as they host the Ball State Fighting David Lettermans. That will be the amuse-bouche of what should be one of the most challenging and entertaining regular seasons that we have seen in many years.

So, as we continue to work our way through the first game week of the season, we have two questions for you in this week's fan survey. First, given the opponents on this fall's schedule, what would you consider a successful regular season? We've put together six options for you to choose from in the survey below.

Then, since the Buckeyes do play this week, we also want you to pick the margin of victory for Saturday's game.

Take a look at the options below, then vote in the survey at the bottom of the article. On Saturday morning, before the game kicks off, we will share the results, so make sure to check back in with us in a few days. And if you want to explain your rationale or add another option, head down to the comments and break it down.

Obviously, we all want the Buckeyes to go undefeated, but I think in the 12-team College Football Playoff Era and in a season with the likes of Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, Oregon, Texas, and USC on the schedule, I think that there is wiggle room for the realistic fans amongst us to entertain the fact that something short of 12-0 could be a success.

Of course, we couldn't make it too straightforward, so the options do have some level of complication mixed in, but I think the results should give us a pretty good insight into where Buckeye Nation's collective head is when it comes to expectations this fall.

This one is a bit easier to digest. The Buckeyes are 50.5-point favorites (which I think is uncomfortably too high, considering they won't want to show anything the week before Texas) and the gold standard of college football analytics SP+ has the game at 60.4 points, which is even more absurd.

Below, I've got a few options for margins of victory for you to choose from. Will Ryan Day, Arthur Smith, and Matt Patricia put up a major ass-kicking to start the season? title: Wisconsin has named its starting running back against Notre Dame
description: Notre Dame found out on Monday which Wisconsin running back will be the starter, and now has almost a week to prepare for him.
fullText:
Wisconsin did not release a depth chart like Notre Dame did for its season opening game, but head coach Luke Fickell did name his starting running back.

The Badgers have a long history of elite play at the position, and its new starter will be Abu Sama as posted on social media by Jesse Temple. The senior played his first three years at Iowa State before transferring in this spring, as he rushed for 1,933-yards with 13 touchdowns during those seasons. He's not much of a receiving threat, with just 20 catches over that time frame.

At 5-foot, 11-inches and 211-pounds, Sama has the ideal size for a back, compact with a lower center of gravity. However, the production hasn't equaled the physique, as he rushed for over 100-yards just once last season in a loss to Colorado. It would be hard to imagine that Sama will have a big day against Notre Dame, considering it is one of the best defenses in the country.

Usage will be a big question, as he had just one game last fall with over 20 carries. Sama doesn't pose a huge threat to the Irish offense, as they now know who they can prepare for on Sunday.

Fickell on the running back room: "I can tell you this, Abu Sama is our 1A. From there, I think there’s a lot of things we’ll have to figure out as we continue to move forward."

Colorado football will open its 2026 home schedule with a refreshed atmosphere at Folsom Field, as CU Athletics introduces new ways for fans to stay involved during games. The first changes will arrive Sept. 12, when Weber State visits Boulder.

title: 'Tremendous work ethic': Texas A&M CB outright earned starting job
description: Texas A&M CB Julio Humphrey put in the work this offseason, winning the No. 2 cornerback job, according to the first depth chart.
fullText:
Entering the 2026 offseason, former Georgia transfer cornerback Julio Humphrey became the forgotten man in a deep cornerback rotation after third-year coach Mike Elko landed a commitment from Tennessee transfer CB Rickey Gibson, who, according to Monday's first 2026 depth chart, is surprisingly in competition for the No. 1 cornerback job with veteran starter Dezz Ricks.

Humphrey's injury-riddled 2025 season did him zero favors entering the offseason, but for those who ever doubted the former blue-chip prospect's work ethic, it's important to remember that he is one of the fastest players on the roster, with the SEC experience to improve his mechanical issues and compete for a starting role.

Outside of junior wide receiver Terry Bussey, the proverbial "drumbeat" was equally loud for Julio Humphrey, who showed vast improvement in man coverage, especially during one of the Aggies' final scrimmages where he and the rest of the cornerback rotation recorded multiple interceptions and pass breakups.

On Monday, after the first depth chart revealed Humphrey as the starting No. 2 cornerback, Mike Elko praised his senior defender, highlighting his aforementioned work ethic and strong fall camp, which outright earned him the opportunity to start from one of the deepest secondaries in the SEC.

"Tremendous work ethic. He has been really, really consistent all through spring, all through summer, all through fall camp," Elko said. "He has gotten a lot more comfortable and confident with what we're asking of him, and that has shone through."

Humphrey's erratic play during his time at Georgia resulted in some fans questioning Elko's decision on Monday, but based on the pervasive use of "OR" designations in the depth chart, Humphrey will need to play at a high and consistent level to keep his starting role, which goes for nearly every player on the roster.
